sentences.zh: 戶皆北向，民居悉覆茅簷，高不得過三尺。

translations.literal: All dwellings face north; common houses are thatched, and their height may not exceed three feet.
translations.idiomatic: Every house faces north; ordinary homes are thatched and may rise no higher than three feet.

sentences.zh: 部領分差等，門高卑亦有限。

translations.literal: Officials differ in rank and grade; the height of doors too is limited.
translations.idiomatic: Officials are graded by rank, and even the height of doorways is regulated.

sentences.zh: 飲食 穢污，魚非腐爛不食，釀不生蛆不為美。

translations.literal: Their food and drink are filthy; they do not eat fish unless it has rotted, and fermented liquor is not considered good unless maggots have bred in it.
translations.idiomatic: Their diet is foul: fish must be rotten before they will eat it, and liquor is prized only when maggots have formed in the brew.

sentences.zh: 人體黑，男蓬頭，女椎結，俱跣足。

translations.literal: Their bodies are black; men wear their hair loose, women in topknots, and all go barefoot.
translations.idiomatic: Their skin is dark; men wear their hair loose, women in topknots, and all go barefoot.

sentences.zh: 王，瑣裡人，崇釋教。

translations.literal: The king is a man of Melaka and reveres Buddhism.
translations.idiomatic: The king is a native of Melaka and a devout Buddhist.

sentences.zh: 歲時採生人膽入酒中，與家人同飲，且以浴身，曰「通 身是膽」。

translations.literal: At seasonal festivals they gather human gall mixed into wine and drink it with family, and also bathe the body in it, saying, "The whole body is gall."
translations.idiomatic: At festival times they mix human gall into wine, drink it with their families, and bathe in it as well, saying, "The whole body is gall."

sentences.zh: 其國人采以獻王，又以洗象目。

translations.literal: The people of the country gather it to present to the king, and also use it to wash elephant eyes.
translations.idiomatic: The people gather gall to offer the king and also use it to wash elephants' eyes.

sentences.zh: 每伺人於道，出不意急殺之，取膽以去。

translations.literal: They lie in wait along the roads, kill people suddenly and unexpectedly, and take the gall before leaving.
translations.idiomatic: They ambush travelers on the roads, kill them without warning, and carry off the gall.

sentences.zh: 若其人驚覺，則膽已先裂，不足用矣。

translations.literal: If the person wakes in alarm, the gall will already have split and cannot be used.
translations.idiomatic: If the victim wakes in fright, the gall bladder will already have burst and be useless.

sentences.zh: 置眾膽於器，華人膽輒居上，故尤貴之。

translations.literal: Many gall bladders are placed in vessels; Chinese gall always rises to the top, and therefore is especially prized.
translations.idiomatic: Gall bladders are stored in vessels; Chinese gall always floats to the top and is therefore most prized.

sentences.zh: 五 六月間，商人出，必戒備。

translations.literal: In the fifth and sixth months, when merchants go out, they must take precautions.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth and sixth months merchants who travel abroad must go on guard.

sentences.zh: 王在位三十年，則避位入深山，以兄弟子侄代，而己持 齋受戒，告於天曰：「我為君無道，願狼虎食我，或病死。」

translations.literal: When the king has reigned thirty years, he abdicates and enters the deep mountains, having brothers' sons and nephews replace him, while he himself observes the fast and receives precepts, declaring to Heaven: "I have ruled without the Way; may wolves and tigers devour me, or may I die of illness."
translations.idiomatic: After thirty years on the throne the king abdicates and withdraws to the deep mountains, leaving a brother's son or nephew to rule while he fasts and takes vows, praying to Heaven: "I have ruled without the Way; may wolves and tigers devour me, or may I die of illness."

sentences.zh: 居一年無恙，則復位 如初。

translations.literal: After dwelling a year unharmed, he resumes the throne as before.
translations.idiomatic: After a year unharmed, he resumed the throne as before.

sentences.zh: 國中呼為「昔嚟馬哈剌」，乃至尊至聖之稱也。

translations.literal: Within the country this is called Xilai Mahala, a title of utmost honor and sanctity.
translations.idiomatic: The realm honors this rite with the title "Xilai Mahala"—the highest and holiest designation.

sentences.zh: 國不甚富，惟犀象最多。

translations.literal: The country is not very wealthy; rhinoceroses and elephants are most numerous.
translations.idiomatic: The country is not especially rich, though rhinoceroses and elephants abound.

sentences.zh: 烏木、降香，樵以為薪。

translations.literal: Ebony and eaglewood—they cut these for firewood.
translations.idiomatic: Ebony and eaglewood are chopped for ordinary firewood.

sentences.zh: 棋柟香獨產其地一山，酋長 遣人守之，民不得采，犯者至斷手。

translations.literal: Chess-nan agarwood grows only on one mountain in their territory; the chief sends men to guard it, and the people may not gather it; violators may have their hands cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Precious chess-nan agarwood grows on a single mountain; the chief posts guards and forbids common gathering—offenders may lose a hand.

sentences.zh: 有鱷魚潭，獄疑不決者，令兩造騎牛過其旁，曲者，魚輒躍而食之，直者，即 數往返，不食也。

translations.literal: There is a crocodile pool; when legal cases are doubtful and unresolved, both parties are made to ride oxen past it—the guilty person, the fish will leap up and eat; the innocent may pass back and forth several times and will not be eaten.
translations.idiomatic: There is a crocodile pool used to settle doubtful cases: both parties ride oxen past it—the guilty are seized and devoured; the innocent may pass back and forth unharmed.

sentences.zh: 有屍頭蠻者，一名屍致魚，本婦人，惟無瞳神為異。

translations.literal: There are flying-head barbarians, also called corpse-raising fish—they are originally women, distinguished only by having no pupils in the eyes.
translations.idiomatic: There are flying-head demons, also called corpse-raising fish—women distinguished only by having no pupils.

sentences.zh: 夜中與人同 寢，忽飛頭食人穢物，來即復活。

translations.literal: At night they sleep with people; suddenly the head flies off to eat human filth, and when it returns the body comes back to life.
translations.idiomatic: At night they sleep beside others; the head suddenly flies off to feed on filth, and when it returns the body lives again.

sentences.zh: 若人知而封其頸，或移之他所，其婦即死。

translations.literal: If people know and seal the neck, or move the body elsewhere, the woman dies.
translations.idiomatic: If someone blocks the neck or moves the body elsewhere, the woman dies.

sentences.zh: 國設 厲禁，有而不告者，罪及一家。

translations.literal: The state maintains strict prohibitions; those who have one in their household and do not report it—the crime extends to the whole family.
translations.idiomatic: The state forbids them strictly; failure to report one in the household punishes the entire family.

sentences.zh: 賓童龍

translations.literal: Panduranga
translations.idiomatic: Panduranga

sentences.zh: 賓童龍國，與占城接壤。

translations.literal: The country of Panduranga borders Champa.
translations.idiomatic: Panduranga borders Champa.

sentences.zh: 或言如來入舍衛國乞食，即其地。

translations.literal: Some say that when the Tathagata entered the kingdom of Shravasti to beg for food, it was this place.
translations.idiomatic: Some hold that this was where the Buddha entered Shravasti to beg alms.

sentences.zh: 氣候、草木、人物、 風土，大類占城，惟遭喪能持服，葬以僻地，設齋禮佛，婚姻偶合。

translations.literal: Climate, plants, people, and customs greatly resemble Champa, except that in mourning they can keep mourning dress, bury in secluded places, set out vegetarian feasts and worship Buddha, and marriages are by mutual agreement.
translations.idiomatic: Climate, flora, people, and customs closely resemble Champa, though mourners observe proper dress, bury the dead in remote places, hold vegetarian feasts and worship Buddha, and marriages are by mutual consent.

sentences.zh: 酋出入乘象或 馬，從者百餘人，前後贊唱。

translations.literal: When the chief goes out he rides an elephant or horse, with over a hundred followers who chant praises before and behind.
translations.idiomatic: The chief travels by elephant or horse with more than a hundred attendants chanting praises before and behind.

sentences.zh: 民編茅覆屋。

translations.literal: The people weave thatch to cover their houses.
translations.idiomatic: The people thatch their houses with woven straw.

sentences.zh: 貨用金、銀、花布。

translations.literal: For currency they use gold, silver, and patterned cloth.
translations.idiomatic: They use gold, silver, and patterned cloth as currency.

sentences.zh: 有崑崙山，節然大海中，與占城及東、西竺鼎峙相望。

translations.literal: There is Kunlun Mountain, standing abruptly in the great sea, facing Champa and the eastern and western Jambudvipas in tripartite confrontation.
translations.idiomatic: Kunlun Mountain rises abruptly from the open sea, facing Champa and the eastern and western lands of India in a three-sided stand.

sentences.zh: 其山方廣而高，其海即 曰崑崙洋。

translations.literal: The mountain is square, broad, and high; the sea there is called the Kunlun Sea.
translations.idiomatic: The mountain is broad, square, and tall; the surrounding waters are called the Kunlun Sea.

sentences.zh: 諸往西洋者，必待順風，七晝夜始得過，故舟人為之諺曰：「上怕七州， 下怕崑崙，針迷舵失，人船莫存。」

translations.literal: All who sail to the Western Ocean must wait for a fair wind; only after seven days and nights can they pass. Therefore sailors have a proverb: "Above one fears the Seven Prefectures; below one fears Kunlun; if the needle is lost and the rudder fails, neither man nor ship survives."
translations.idiomatic: All who sail west must wait for fair winds and need seven days and nights to pass. Sailors have a proverb: "Above one fears the Seven Prefectures; below one fears Kunlun; lose the needle and rudder, and neither man nor ship survives."

sentences.zh: 此山無異產。

translations.literal: This mountain has no unusual products.
translations.idiomatic: The mountain yielded nothing of note.

sentences.zh: 人皆穴居巢處，食果實魚蝦，無室廬井灶。

translations.literal: The people all dwell in caves and nests, eat fruit, fish, and shrimp, and have no houses, wells, or hearths.
translations.idiomatic: They live in caves and treetop shelters, eating fruit, fish, and shrimp, with no proper houses, wells, or stoves.

sentences.zh: 真臘，在占城南，順風三晝夜可至。

translations.literal: Chenla lies south of Champa; with a fair wind one can reach it in three days and nights.
translations.idiomatic: Chenla lies south of Champa—a fair wind brings you there in three days and nights.

sentences.zh: 隋、唐及宋皆朝貢。

translations.literal: Under Sui, Tang, and Song it all sent tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Sui, Tang, and Song dynasties it sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 宋慶元中，滅占城而 並其地，因改國名曰占臘。

translations.literal: In the Qingyuan era of Song it destroyed Champa and annexed its territory, therefore changing the state name to Zhanla.
translations.idiomatic: During Song Qingyuan it conquered Champa and annexed its lands, renaming the realm Zhanla.

sentences.zh: 元時仍稱真臘。

translations.literal: Under Yuan it was again called Chenla.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Yuan it was again called Chenla.

sentences.zh: 洪武三年，遣使臣郭徵等齎詔撫諭其國。

translations.literal: In the third year of Hongwu, envoys led by Guo Zheng were dispatched bearing an edict to soothe and instruct the country.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 3 envoys led by Guo Zheng were sent with an edict to reassure and instruct the realm.

sentences.zh: 四年，其國巴山王忽爾那遣使進表， 貢方物，賀明年正旦。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Basan Wang Hu'erna of that country sent envoys with a memorial, presenting local products and congratulating the New Year of the following year.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 4 Basan Wang Hu'erna sent envoys with a memorial, local products, and New Year's greetings for the coming year.

sentences.zh: 詔賜《大統歷》及彩幣，使者亦給賜有差。

translations.literal: An edict bestowed the Datong Calendar and patterned silks; the envoys also received graded gifts.
translations.idiomatic: The court granted the Datong Calendar and patterned silks; the envoys received graded gifts as well.

sentences.zh: 六年進貢。

translations.literal: In the sixth year they entered tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 6 they sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 十二 年，王參答甘武者持達志遣使來貢，宴賜如前。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, King Samdach Gamwat Houdet sent envoys to offer tribute; feasts and gifts were as before.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 12 King Samdach Gamwat Houdet sent tribute envoys; feasts and gifts followed the earlier precedent.

sentences.zh: 十三年復貢。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year they again offered tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 13 they sent tribute again.

sentences.zh: 十六年遣使齎勘合文 冊賜其王。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year envoys were sent bearing tally slips and credential booklets to bestow on the king.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 16 envoys were dispatched with tally slips and credential documents for the king.

sentences.zh: 凡國中使至，勘合不符者，即屬矯偽，許縶縛以聞。

translations.literal: Whenever envoys from the country arrived, if the tally did not match, they were deemed fraudulent and might be bound and reported.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever envoys arrived, mismatched tallies marked them as impostors, who might be bound and reported.

sentences.zh: 復遣使賜織金文綺 三十二、磁器萬九千。

translations.literal: Envoys were again sent bearing thirty-two pieces of brocaded silk and nineteen thousand pieces of porcelain.
translations.idiomatic: More envoys were sent bearing thirty-two lengths of brocaded silk and nineteen thousand pieces of porcelain.

sentences.zh: 其王遣使來貢。

translations.literal: The king sent envoys to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: The king sent tribute envoys.

sentences.zh: 十九年遣行人劉敏、唐敬偕中官齎磁器往賜。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year Commissioner Liu Min and Tang Jing were sent together with eunuchs bearing porcelain as gifts.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 19 Commissioners Liu Min and Tang Jing went with eunuchs bearing porcelain gifts.

sentences.zh: 明年，敬等還，王遣使貢象五十九、香六萬斤。

translations.literal: The next year Jing and the others returned; the king sent envoys offering fifty-nine elephants and sixty thousand jin of incense.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, when Jing's party returned, the king sent fifty-nine elephants and sixty thousand jin of incense as tribute.

sentences.zh: 尋遣使賜其王鍍金銀印，王及妃皆 有賜。

translations.literal: Soon envoys were sent bestowing a gilt silver seal on the king; both the king and consort received gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Soon envoys were sent with a gilt silver seal for the king; both king and consort received gifts.

sentences.zh: 其王參烈實{田比}邪甘菩者遣使貢象及方物。

translations.literal: King Samleak Piphey Kamphea sent envoys offering elephants and local products.
translations.idiomatic: King Samleak Piphey Kamphea sent envoys with elephants and local products.

sentences.zh: 明年復貢像二十八、象奴三十 四人、番奴四十五人，謝賜印之恩。

translations.literal: The next year they again offered twenty-eight elephant statues, thirty-four elephant keepers, and forty-five foreign slaves, thanking for the gift of the seal.
translations.idiomatic: The next year they sent twenty-eight elephant statues, thirty-four elephant keepers, and forty-five foreign slaves in thanks for the seal.

sentences.zh: 二十二年三貢。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year they offered tribute three times.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 22 they sent tribute three times.

sentences.zh: 明年復貢。

translations.literal: The next year they again offered tribute.
translations.idiomatic: The following year they sent tribute again.

sentences.zh: 永樂元年，遣行人蔣賓興、王樞以即位詔諭其國。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongle, Attendants Jiang Binxing and Wang Shu were sent with an accession edict to instruct the state.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle 1, Attendants Jiang Binxing and Wang Shu were sent with an accession edict to notify the kingdom.

sentences.zh: 明年，王參烈婆田比牙遣使來朝，貢方物。

translations.literal: The next year, King Samleak Piphey sent envoys to court and offered local products.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, King Samleak Piphey sent envoys to court with local products.

sentences.zh: 初，中官使真臘，有部卒三人潛遁，索之不得，王以其國三人代之，至是引見。

translations.literal: Earlier, when a eunuch envoy visited Chenla, three of his attendants fled in secret and could not be found; the king substituted three men of his own country, and at this time they were presented.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when a eunuch envoy visited Chenla, three attendants fled and could not be recovered; the king supplied three of his own subjects in their place, and they were now presented.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「華人自逃，於彼何預而責償？

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Chinese subjects fled on their own—what has that to do with them, that compensation should be demanded?
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "These Chinese fled on their own. What has that to do with them, that you should demand compensation?

sentences.zh: 且語言不通，風土不習，吾焉用之？」

translations.literal: Moreover, their language is not understood and they are unaccustomed to the local ways—what use have I for them?"
translations.idiomatic: Besides, they do not speak the language and are unused to the land—what use would I have for them?"

sentences.zh: 命賜衣服及道里費，遣還。

translations.literal: He ordered clothes and travel expenses to be granted and sent them back.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered clothes and travel expenses given and sent them home.

sentences.zh: 三年遣使來貢，告故王之喪。

translations.literal: In the third year envoys came with tribute and reported the former king's death.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year envoys came with tribute to report the former king's death.

sentences.zh: 命鴻臚序班王孜致祭，給事中畢進、中官王琮齎詔封其嗣子參烈昭平牙為王。

translations.literal: He ordered Ceremonial Reception Clerk Wang Zi to perform the mourning rites, and Supervising Secretary Bi Jin and eunuch Wang Cong to bear an edict enfeoffing his heir Samleak Cheab Piphey as king.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Ceremonial Reception Clerk Wang Zi to perform the mourning rites, and Supervising Secretary Bi Jin and eunuch Wang Cong to carry an edict enfeoffing the heir Samleak Cheab Piphey as king.

sentences.zh: 進等還，嗣王遣使偕來謝恩。

translations.literal: When Jin and the others returned, the new king sent envoys together with them to express gratitude.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin's party returned, the new king sent envoys with them to give thanks.

sentences.zh: 六年、十二年再入貢。

translations.literal: In the sixth and twelfth years they again entered with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: They sent tribute again in the sixth and twelfth years.

sentences.zh: 使者以其國數被占城侵擾，久留不去。

translations.literal: The envoys, because their country had repeatedly been harassed by Champa, remained long and did not depart.
translations.idiomatic: Because their country had been repeatedly harassed by Champa, the envoys lingered and would not leave.

sentences.zh: 帝遣中官送之還，並敕占城王罷兵修好。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent a eunuch to escort them home and also ordered the king of Champa to cease troops and restore friendly relations.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sent a eunuch to escort them home and ordered the king of Champa to cease hostilities and restore friendly relations.

sentences.zh: 十五年、十七年併入貢。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth and seventeenth years they again entered with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: They sent tribute again in the fifteenth and seventeenth years.

sentences.zh: 宣德、景泰中，亦遣使入貢。

translations.literal: During the Xuande and Jingtai reigns they also sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xuande and Jingtai reigns they also sent tribute envoys.

sentences.zh: 自後不常至。

translations.literal: After that they did not come regularly.
translations.idiomatic: After that they no longer came regularly.

sentences.zh: 其國城隍周七十餘里，幅員廣數千里。

translations.literal: The country's walled city circumference is over seventy li; its territory extends thousands of li in breadth.
translations.idiomatic: The capital's walls run more than seventy li; the realm spans thousands of li.

sentences.zh: 國中有金塔、金橋、殿宇三十餘所。

translations.literal: Within the country are golden pagodas, golden bridges, and over thirty halls.
translations.idiomatic: Golden pagodas, golden bridges, and more than thirty palace halls stand within the realm.

sentences.zh: 王 歲時一會，羅列玉猿、孔雀、白象、犀牛於前，名曰百塔洲。

translations.literal: Once a year the king holds a great assembly, arraying jade gibbons, peacocks, white elephants, and rhinoceroses before him—a place called Hundred Pagoda Province.
translations.idiomatic: Each year the king holds a great assembly, displaying jade gibbons, peacocks, white elephants, and rhinoceroses at a place called Hundred Pagoda Province.

sentences.zh: 盛食以金盤、金椀， 故有「富貴真臘」之諺。

translations.literal: Food is served on golden plates and bowls; hence the proverb "Prosperous Chenla."
translations.idiomatic: Meals are served on gold plates and bowls—hence the saying "Prosperous Chenla."

sentences.zh: 民俗富饒。

translations.literal: The customs of the people are wealthy and abundant.
translations.idiomatic: The people live in abundance.

sentences.zh: 天時常熱，不識霜雪，禾一歲數稔。

translations.literal: The weather is always hot; they know neither frost nor snow; grain ripens several times a year.
translations.idiomatic: The climate is perpetually hot, with no frost or snow; grain ripens several times a year.

sentences.zh: 男女椎結， 穿短衫，圍梢布。

translations.literal: Men and women wear topknots, short jackets, and wrap sarongs.
translations.idiomatic: Men and women wear topknots, short jackets, and wrap sarongs about the waist.

sentences.zh: 刑有劓、刖、刺配，盜則去手足。

translations.literal: Punishments include nose-cutting, foot-cutting, and tattooing with exile; thieves have hands and feet removed.
translations.idiomatic: Punishments include nose-cutting, mutilation, tattooing and exile; thieves lose hands and feet.

sentences.zh: 番人殺唐人罪死；

translations.literal: If a foreigner kills a Tang person, the penalty is death;
translations.idiomatic: If a native kills a Chinese, the penalty is death;

sentences.zh: 唐人殺番人 則罰金，無金則鬻身贖罪。

translations.literal: if a Tang person kills a foreigner, the penalty is a fine; if there is no gold, the body is sold to redeem the crime.
translations.idiomatic: if a Chinese kills a native, the penalty is a fine—or, without gold, enslavement to pay the debt.

sentences.zh: 唐人者，諸番呼華人之稱也，凡海外諸國盡然。

translations.literal: Tang person is what all foreign states call Chinese; this is so for every country beyond the sea.
translations.idiomatic: Tang ren is what every foreign state calls the Chinese—a usage common across the overseas realms.

sentences.zh: 婚嫁， 兩傢俱八日不出門，晝夜燃燈。

translations.literal: For marriage, both families stay indoors for eight days without going out, and lamps burn day and night.
translations.idiomatic: At weddings both families remain indoors for eight days, lamps burning day and night.

sentences.zh: 人死置於野，任烏鳶食，俄頃食盡者，謂為福報。

translations.literal: When a person dies the body is placed in the open country and left to vultures and kites; if it is consumed in a moment, this is called blessed reward.
translations.idiomatic: The dead are left in the open for vultures and kites; swift consumption counts as blessed merit.

sentences.zh: 居喪，但髡其發，女子則額上剪髮如錢大，曰用此報親。

translations.literal: In mourning one only shaves the hair; women clip the hair on the forehead to the size of a coin, saying this repays the parents.
translations.idiomatic: In mourning men shave their heads; women clip a coin-sized patch of hair on the forehead, calling it repayment to their parents.

sentences.zh: 文字以麂鹿雜皮染黑，用 粉為小條畫於上，永不脫落。

translations.literal: For writing they use deerskin and mixed hides dyed black; fine strips of powder are drawn on them and never fall off.
translations.idiomatic: Writing is done on deerskin and other hides dyed black, with powdered strokes that never fade.

sentences.zh: 以十月為歲首，閏悉用九月。

translations.literal: The tenth month is taken as the start of the year; intercalary months are all placed in the ninth month.
translations.idiomatic: The year begins in the tenth month; intercalary months are always inserted in the ninth.

sentences.zh: 夜分四更。

translations.literal: Night is divided into four watches.
translations.idiomatic: The night is divided into four watches.

sentences.zh: 亦有曉天文 者，能算日月薄蝕。

translations.literal: There are also those who understand astronomy and can calculate solar and lunar eclipses.
translations.idiomatic: Some understand astronomy and can calculate eclipses of the sun and moon.

sentences.zh: 其地謂儒為班詰，僧為苧姑，道為八思。

translations.literal: In that land Confucians are called banjie, Buddhist monks are called chugu, and Taoists are called basi.
translations.idiomatic: There Confucians are called banjie, Buddhist monks chugu, and Taoists basi.

sentences.zh: 班詰不知讀何書，由 此入仕者為華貫。

translations.literal: The banjie do not know what books they read; those who enter office by this path hold the highest civil honors.
translations.idiomatic: The banjie read no identifiable canon, yet those who rise through their ranks hold the highest civil posts.

sentences.zh: 先時項掛一白線以自別，既貴曳白如故。

translations.literal: Formerly they hung a white thread at the neck to distinguish themselves; once elevated they still drag white as before.
translations.idiomatic: Once they wore a white cord at the neck to mark their station; even after promotion they still trailed white.

sentences.zh: 俗尚釋教，僧皆食魚、 肉，或以供佛，惟不飲酒。

translations.literal: The custom honors Buddhism; monks all eat fish and meat, or offer them to Buddha, but only do not drink wine.
translations.idiomatic: Buddhism is widely honored; monks eat fish and meat—or offer them to the Buddha—but abstain from wine alone.

sentences.zh: 其國自稱甘孛智，後訛為甘破蔗，萬曆後又改為柬埔寨。

translations.literal: The country calls itself Ganbozhi; later this was corrupted to Ganpozhe, and after Wanli again changed to Jianpuzhai.
translations.idiomatic: The realm calls itself Kambuja, later corrupted to Kampuchea, and after Wanli became Cambodia.

sentences.zh: 暹羅，在占城西南，順風十晝夜可至，即隋、唐赤土國。

translations.literal: Siam lies southwest of Champa; with a fair wind one can reach it in ten days and nights—it is the Red Earth country of Sui and Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Siam lies southwest of Champa—ten days and nights with a fair wind—the Red Earth kingdom of Sui and Tang times.

sentences.zh: 後分為羅斛、暹二國。

translations.literal: Later it split into the two states of Lohu and Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Later it divided into the two realms of Lohu and Siam.

sentences.zh: 暹土瘠不宜稼，羅斛地平衍，種多獲，暹仰給焉。

translations.literal: Siam's soil is barren and unsuitable for grain; Lohu's land is flat and open, planting yields abundant harvests, and Siam relies on it for its supply.
translations.idiomatic: Siam's soil was too poor for grain, but Lohu's plains were fertile and yielded rich harvests, and Siam depended on it for food.

sentences.zh: 元時，暹常入貢。

translations.literal: During Yuan times, Siam often sent tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Yuan, Siam regularly sent tribute missions.

sentences.zh: 其後，羅斛強， 並有暹地，遂稱暹羅斛國。

translations.literal: Afterward Lohu grew strong, annexed Siam's territory as well, and thus was styled the state of Siam-Lohu.
translations.idiomatic: Later Lohu grew powerful, absorbed Siam's lands, and came to be called the kingdom of Siam-Lohu.

sentences.zh: 洪武三年，命使臣呂宗俊等齎詔諭其國。

translations.literal: In the third year of Hongwu, envoys including Lü Zongjun were ordered to carry an edict announcing instructions to their state.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 3, the court dispatched envoys led by Lü Zongjun to bear an edict to the kingdom.

sentences.zh: 四年，其王參烈昭{田比}牙遣使奉表， 與宗俊等偕來，貢馴象、六足龜及方物，詔賜其王錦綺及使者幣帛有差。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, King Samleak Pipiya sent envoys presenting a memorial, arriving together with Zongjun and the others, offering tame elephants, six-legged tortoises, and local products; an edict bestowed patterned silks upon the king and graded silk gifts upon the envoys.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, King Samleak Pipiya sent envoys with a memorial, arriving with Zongjun's party. They offered tame elephants, six-legged tortoises, and local goods. The court granted the king brocades and rewarded the envoys with silks in graded amounts.

sentences.zh: 已，復遣 使賀明年正旦，詔賜《大統歷》及彩幣。

translations.literal: Soon afterward, he again sent envoys to congratulate the coming New Year's Day; an edict bestowed the Datong Calendar and colored silks.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he sent envoys again to felicitate the coming New Year. The court granted them the Datong Calendar and colored silks.

sentences.zh: 五年貢黑熊、白猿及方物。

translations.literal: In the fifth year they offered black bears, white gibbons, and local products.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year they sent black bears, white gibbons, and local products as tribute.

sentences.zh: 明年復來貢。

translations.literal: The next year they came again with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: The following year they sent tribute again.

sentences.zh: 其王之姊參烈思寧別遣使進金葉表，貢方物於中宮，卻之。

translations.literal: The king's elder sister Samleak Sinning separately sent envoys presenting a gold-leaf memorial and offering local products to the empress; it was declined.
translations.idiomatic: The king's elder sister Samleak Sinning separately sent envoys with a gold-leaf memorial and local products for the empress. The court refused them.

sentences.zh: 已而其姊復遣使來貢， 帝仍卻之，而宴賚其使。

translations.literal: Soon after, his sister again sent envoys with tribute; the Emperor still declined it, but feasted and rewarded the envoys.
translations.idiomatic: His sister sent tribute again soon after. The Emperor once more refused the gifts but entertained and rewarded her envoys.

sentences.zh: 時其王懦而不武，國人推其伯父參烈寶毘邪哩哆囉祿主國事，遣使來告，貢方物，宴賚如制。

translations.literal: At the time the king was timid and not martial; the people of the state pushed his uncle Samleak Piphet Sisili Duoluolu to manage state affairs. He sent envoys to report this, offered local products, and received feasts and rewards according to regulation.
translations.idiomatic: The king was weak and unwarlike, so the people installed his uncle Samleak Piphet Sisili Duoluolu to govern. He sent envoys to inform the court, presented local goods, and was feasted and rewarded as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 已而新王遣使來貢、謝恩，其使者 亦有獻，帝不納。

translations.literal: Before long the new king sent envoys with tribute and to express gratitude; his envoys also made offerings, but the Emperor did not accept them.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the new king sent envoys with tribute and thanks. They brought additional gifts as well, but the Emperor declined them.

sentences.zh: 已，遣使賀明年正旦，貢方物，且獻本國地圖。

translations.literal: Soon afterward, he sent envoys to congratulate the coming New Year's Day, offered local products, and also presented a map of his state.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent envoys to felicitate the coming New Year, bearing local products and a map of his kingdom.

sentences.zh: 七年，使臣沙裡拔來貢。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, the envoy Shaliba came with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, the envoy Shaliba arrived with tribute.

sentences.zh: 言去年舟次烏豬洋，遭風壞舟，飄至海南，賴官司救 護，尚存飄余兜羅綿、降香、蘇木諸物進獻，廣東省臣以聞。

translations.literal: He reported that last year, when his ship anchored at Wuzhu Yang, it was wrecked by wind, drifted to Hainan, and thanks to official rescue and protection, what remained of the drifted cargo—tuluo cotton, agarwood, sappanwood, and other goods—was presented; the Guangdong provincial officials reported this.
translations.idiomatic: He reported that the previous year his vessel had anchored at Wuzhu Yang, been wrecked in a storm, and drifted to Hainan. Officials had rescued the party, and he now presented what survived of the cargo—kapok, agarwood, sappanwood, and the like. The Guangdong authorities reported the matter.

sentences.zh: 帝怪其無表，既言舟 覆，而方物乃有存者，疑其為番商，命卻之。

translations.literal: The Emperor wondered that he had no memorial; since he said the ship had capsized, yet local products still survived, he suspected them to be foreign merchants and ordered the gifts declined.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor found it strange that he brought no memorial. If the ship had truly capsized, how could tribute goods remain? Suspecting foreign merchants, he ordered the offerings refused.

sentences.zh: 諭中書及禮部臣曰：「古諸侯於天子， 比年一小聘，三年一大聘。

translations.literal: He instructed the Secretariat and Ministry of Rites officials, saying: "In antiquity, feudal lords toward the Son of Heaven paid a minor visit every other year and a major visit every three years.
translations.idiomatic: He told officials of the Secretariat and Ministry of Rites: "In ancient times, feudal lords paid the Son of Heaven a minor visit every other year and a major visit every three years.

sentences.zh: 九州之外，則每世一朝，所貢方物，表誠敬而已。

translations.literal: Beyond the Nine Provinces, each generation paid one court visit; the local products offered merely expressed sincerity and respect.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond the Nine Provinces, states came to court once a generation; their tribute was only a token of loyalty and respect.

sentences.zh: 惟高 麗頗知禮樂，故令三年一貢。

translations.literal: Only Goryeo was fairly versed in ritual and music, so it was ordered to send tribute once every three years.
translations.idiomatic: Goryeo alone was reasonably well versed in ritual and music, so it alone was allowed tribute every three years.

sentences.zh: 他遠國，如占城、安南、西洋瑣裡、爪哇、浡泥、三 佛齊、暹羅斛、真臘諸國，入貢既頻，勞費太甚。

translations.literal: Other distant states, such as Champa, Annam, Western Ocean Semudera, Java, Brunei, Srivijaya, Siam-Lohu, and Khmer, have been sending tribute so frequently that the labor and expense are excessive.
translations.idiomatic: Other distant realms—Champa, Annam, Semudera in the Western Ocean, Java, Brunei, Srivijaya, Siam-Lohu, Khmer, and the like—have been sending tribute so often that the burden has grown too heavy.

sentences.zh: 今不必復爾，其移牒諸國俾知之。」

translations.literal: Henceforth this need not be so again; dispatch notices to the various states to make them know."
translations.idiomatic: That practice should not continue. Send notices to all these kingdoms so they understand."

sentences.zh: 然而來者不止。

translations.literal: Yet those who came did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: Even so, the tribute missions did not stop.

sentences.zh: 其世子蘇門邦王昭祿群膺亦遣使上箋於皇太子，貢方物。

translations.literal: The crown prince of Sumenbang, Zhaolu Quanying, also sent envoys presenting a letter to the crown prince and offering local products.
translations.idiomatic: The Sumenbang prince Zhaolu Quanying also sent envoys with a letter to the heir apparent and local products.

sentences.zh: 命引其使 朝東宮，宴賚遣之。

translations.literal: An order was issued to lead his envoys to attend upon the Eastern Palace; they were feasted, rewarded, and sent away.
translations.idiomatic: The court had his envoys received at the Eastern Palace, entertained them, rewarded them, and sent them home.

sentences.zh: 八年再入貢。

translations.literal: In the eighth year they sent tribute again.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year they sent tribute once more.

sentences.zh: 其舊明台王世子昭孛羅局亦遣使奉表朝貢，宴賚 如王使。

translations.literal: The crown prince of the former Mingtai, Zhaobo Luo Ju, also sent envoys presenting a memorial and paying court tribute; feasts and rewards were the same as for the king's envoys.
translations.idiomatic: The former Mingtai prince Zhaobo Luo Ju also sent envoys with a memorial and tribute. They were feasted and rewarded like the king's own envoys.

sentences.zh: 十年，昭祿群膺承其父命來朝。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, Zhaolu Quanying came to court on his father's orders.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year, Zhaolu Quanying came to court at his father's command.

sentences.zh: 帝喜，命禮部員外郎王恆等齎詔及印賜之，文 曰「暹羅國王之印」，並賜世子衣幣及道里費。

translations.literal: The Emperor was pleased and ordered Supervising Secretary Wang Heng and others to carry an edict and seal to bestow upon him; the inscription read "Seal of the King of Siam," and the crown prince was also granted robes, silks, and travel expenses.
translations.idiomatic: Delighted, the Emperor ordered Wang Heng of the Ministry of Rites and others to bear an edict and seal. The inscription read "Seal of the King of Siam," and the prince received robes, silks, and travel funds as well.

sentences.zh: 自是，其國遵朝命，始稱暹羅；

translations.literal: From this time, the state obeyed the court's command and first styled itself Siam;
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, following the court's command, the kingdom took the name Siam;

sentences.zh: 比 年一貢，或一年兩貢。

translations.literal: tribute came once every other year, or twice in one year.
translations.idiomatic: it sent tribute every other year, or sometimes twice in a single year.

sentences.zh: 至正統後，或數年一貢雲。

translations.literal: From the Zhengtong reign onward, tribute sometimes came only once every several years.
translations.idiomatic: After the Zhengtong era, missions might come only once every few years.

sentences.zh: 十六年，賜勘合文冊及文綺、磁器，與真臘等。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, tally documents, patterned silks, and porcelain were bestowed, as with Khmer and others.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year, the court granted tally documents, brocades, and porcelain, as it did for Khmer and the rest.

sentences.zh: 二十年貢胡椒一萬斤、蘇木一 萬斤。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year they offered ten thousand jin of pepper and ten thousand jin of sappanwood.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year they sent ten thousand jin of pepper and ten thousand jin of sappanwood.

sentences.zh: 帝遣官厚報之。

translations.literal: The Emperor dispatched officials to reward them generously in return.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sent officials to return rich gifts.

sentences.zh: 時溫州民有市其沉香諸物者，所司坐以通番，當棄市。

translations.literal: At the time, Wenzhou commoners who had purchased their agarwood and other goods were charged by the authorities with illicit foreign trade and sentenced to execution at the market.
translations.idiomatic: Some Wenzhou residents who had bought the envoys' agarwood and other goods were charged with illegal foreign trade and condemned to death.

sentences.zh: 帝曰： 「溫州乃暹羅必經之地，因其往來而市之，非通番也。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Wenzhou is a place Siam must pass through on its journeys; because they trade as the envoys come and go, this is not illicit foreign trade."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "Wenzhou lies on Siam's regular route. Trading with envoys as they pass through is not illicit foreign commerce."

sentences.zh: 乃獲宥。

translations.literal: They were therefore pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: The men were pardoned.

sentences.zh: 二十一，年貢象 三十、番奴六十。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year they offered thirty elephants and sixty foreign slaves.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year they sent thirty elephants and sixty foreign slaves.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，世子昭祿群膺遣使來貢。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year, the crown prince Zhaolu Quanying sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year, Crown Prince Zhaolu Quanying sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 二十三，年貢蘇木、胡椒、 降香十七萬斤。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year they offered one hundred seventy thousand jin of sappanwood, pepper, and agarwood.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year they sent one hundred seventy thousand jin of sappanwood, pepper, and agarwood.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，昭祿群膺遣使朝貢，且告父喪。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year, Zhaolu Quanying sent envoys to pay court tribute and report his father's death.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year, Zhaolu Quanying sent envoys with tribute and news of his father's death.

sentences.zh: 命中官趙達等往祭，敕世子嗣王位， 賜賚有加。

translations.literal: Eunuchs including Zhao Da were ordered to go and perform the mourning rites; the crown prince was commanded to succeed to the kingship, and additional rewards were bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent eunuchs led by Zhao Da to perform mourning rites, confirmed the crown prince as king, and granted him extra gifts.

sentences.zh: 諭曰：「朕自即位以來，命使出疆，周於四維，足履其境者三十六，聲 聞於耳者三十一，風殊俗異。

translations.literal: An instruction read: "Since I ascended the throne, I have dispatched envoys beyond the borders, reaching all four quarters; thirty-six states have been trodden by foot, thirty-one heard of by ear—customs differ and ways diverge.
translations.idiomatic: The edict read: "Since my accession I have sent envoys in every direction. Thirty-six realms my envoys have entered on foot, thirty-one more known by report—each with its own customs and ways.

sentences.zh: 大國十有八，小國百四十九，較之於今，暹羅最近。

translations.literal: Great states number eighteen, small states one hundred forty-nine; compared with the present, Siam is nearest.
translations.idiomatic: There are eighteen great kingdoms and one hundred forty-nine lesser ones; of them all, Siam is the closest to us now.

sentences.zh: 邇者使至，知爾先王已逝。

translations.literal: Your envoys have lately arrived, and I know your late king has passed away.
translations.idiomatic: Your envoys have just arrived with word that your late king has died.

sentences.zh: 王紹先三之緒，有道於邦家，臣民懽懌。

translations.literal: The king inherits the line of his three predecessors; he has the Way in his state and household, and officials and people rejoice.
translations.idiomatic: You succeed the line of three generations of kings, govern your realm with virtue, and your subjects rejoice.

sentences.zh: 茲特遣人錫命， 王其罔失法度，罔淫於樂，以光前烈。

translations.literal: Now I specially send men to grant the mandate: the king must not lose the laws and standards, must not indulge in pleasure, and thereby glorify the achievements of his forebears.
translations.idiomatic: I now send envoys to invest you: hold fast to law and measure, do not sink into dissipation, and so honor your forefathers' legacy.

sentences.zh: 欽哉。」

translations.literal: Reverently heed this."
translations.idiomatic: Take heed."

sentences.zh: 成祖即位，詔諭其國。

translations.literal: When the Yongle Emperor ascended the throne, he issued an edict to instruct their state.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yongle Emperor took the throne, he sent an edict to their country.

sentences.zh: 永樂元年賜 其王昭祿群膺哆囉諦剌駝紐鍍金銀印，其王即遣使謝恩。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongle, King Zhaolu Quanying Duoluodilatuoniu was granted a gilded silver seal; the king immediately sent envoys to express gratitude.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle 1, King Zhaolu Quanying Duoluodilatuoniu received a gilded silver seal, and he at once sent envoys to give thanks.

sentences.zh: 六月，以上高皇帝尊謚， 遣官頒詔，有賜。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, because of the posthumous title of the High Emperor, officials were dispatched to promulgate an edict, with gifts.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, officials were sent to proclaim the late Hongwu Emperor's posthumous title, bearing gifts.

sentences.zh: 八月覆命給事中王哲、行人成務賜其王錦綺。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, upon their return, Supervising Secretary Wang Zhe and Attendant Cheng Wu were sent to bestow patterned silks upon the king.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, when the envoys returned, Wang Zhe of the Secretariat and Attendant Cheng Wu were sent to grant the king brocades.

sentences.zh: 九月命中官李興等 齎敕，勞賜其王，其文武諸臣並有賜。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, eunuchs including Li Xing were ordered to carry an imperial letter, console and reward the king, and his civil and military officials all received gifts as well.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, eunuchs led by Li Xing bore an imperial letter of consolation and reward for the king; his civil and military officials received gifts too.

sentences.zh: 二年有番船飄至福建海岸，詰之，乃暹羅與琉球通好者。

translations.literal: In the second year a foreign ship drifted to the Fujian coast; upon inquiry, it proved to be one traveling in friendship between Siam and Ryukyu.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year a foreign vessel was driven onto the Fujian coast. Questioning showed it was bound in amity between Siam and Ryukyu.

sentences.zh: 所司籍其貨以聞，帝 曰：「二國修好，乃甚美事，不幸遭風，正宜憐惜，豈可因以為利。

translations.literal: The responsible officials registered its cargo and reported; the Emperor said: "That the two states are on good terms is a very fine thing. Misfortune by wind should rightly be pitied—how could one profit from it?
translations.idiomatic: Officials inventoried the cargo and reported up. The Emperor said: "Friendship between the two kingdoms is a fine thing. A ship wrecked by storm deserves pity, not profit.

sentences.zh: 所司其治舟給 粟，俟風便遣赴琉球。」

translations.literal: Let the responsible officials repair the ship, supply grain, and wait for a favorable wind before sending them on to Ryukyu."
translations.idiomatic: Repair their vessel, give them grain, and when the winds allow send them on to Ryukyu."

sentences.zh: 是月，其王以帝降璽書勞賜，遣使來謝，貢方物。

translations.literal: That month, because the Emperor had sent an imperial letter of consolation and reward, the king dispatched envoys to express thanks and offer local products.
translations.idiomatic: That same month, grateful for the Emperor's letter of reward, the king sent envoys with thanks and local products.

sentences.zh: 賜齎有 加，並賜《列女傳》百冊。

translations.literal: The gifts bestowed were increased, and one hundred volumes of the Biographies of Exemplary Women were also granted.
translations.idiomatic: The return gifts were increased, and the court also granted one hundred copies of the Biographies of Exemplary Women.

sentences.zh: 使者請頒量衡為國永式，從之。

translations.literal: The envoys requested that weights and measures be issued as the kingdom's permanent standard; the request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The envoys asked for official weights and measures to serve as permanent standards for their kingdom. The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 先是，占城貢使返，風飄其舟至彭亨，暹羅索取其使，羈留不遣。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Champa's tribute envoys were returning, wind drove their ship to Pahang; Siam demanded their envoys and detained them without releasing them.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Champa tribute envoys returning home were blown off course to Pahang. Siam seized them and refused to release them.

sentences.zh: 蘇門答剌及 滿剌加又訴暹羅恃強發兵奪天朝所賜印誥。

translations.literal: Samudera and Malacca also complained that Siam, relying on its strength, had raised troops and seized the seals and patents bestowed by the Celestial Court.
translations.idiomatic: Samudera and Malacca also accused Siam of using its power to send troops and seize the seals and patents the Celestial Court had granted them.

sentences.zh: 帝降敕責之曰：「占城、蘇門答剌、滿 剌加與爾俱受朝命，安得逞威拘其貢使，奪其誥印。

translations.literal: The Emperor issued an imperial rebuke, saying: "Champa, Samudera, and Malacca, like you, all received court mandates—how dare you wield power, detain their tribute envoys, and seize their patents and seals?
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sent a stern rebuke: "Champa, Samudera, and Malacca, like you, all hold mandates from the court. How dare you bully them, hold their envoys, and steal their patents and seals?

sentences.zh: 天有顯道，福善禍淫，安南黎 賊可為鑑戒。

translations.literal: Heaven has a manifest Way: fortune follows the good and calamity the wicked—the Lei rebels of Annam may serve as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's way is clear: virtue is rewarded and wickedness punished. The Le usurpers of Annam should be your warning.

sentences.zh: 其即返占城使者，還蘇門答剌、滿剌加印誥。

translations.literal: Immediately return Champa's envoys and restore the patents and seals of Samudera and Malacca.
translations.idiomatic: Return Champa's envoys at once and give back Samudera's and Malacca's patents and seals.

sentences.zh: 自今奉法循理，保境睦 鄰，庶永享太平之福。」

translations.literal: From now on observe the law and follow reason, preserve your borders and live in harmony with neighbors, and you may long enjoy the blessings of peace."
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth keep the law, guard your borders, and live at peace with your neighbors if you wish to enjoy lasting tranquility."

sentences.zh: 時暹羅所遣貢使，失風飄至安南，盡為黎賊所殺，止余孛 黑一人。

translations.literal: At the time, tribute envoys sent by Siam were blown off course to Annam and were all killed by the Lei rebels; only one man, Bo Hei, remained.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile, Siam's tribute envoys had been blown to Annam and slaughtered by the Le rebels; only Bo Hei survived.

sentences.zh: 後官軍征安南，獲之以歸。

translations.literal: Later, when the imperial army campaigned against Annam, he was captured and brought back.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial army later campaigned in Annam, he was captured and brought home.

sentences.zh: 帝憫之，六年八月命中官張原送還國，賜王幣 帛，令厚恤被殺者之家。

translations.literal: The Emperor took pity on him; in the eighth month of the sixth year he ordered the eunuch Zhang Yuan to escort him back to his state, bestowed silks upon the king, and commanded that the families of those killed be generously compensated.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor took pity on him. In the eighth month of the sixth year he sent eunuch Zhang Yuan to escort him home, granted silks to the king, and ordered generous compensation for the families of the slain envoys.

sentences.zh: 九月，中官鄭和使其國，其王遣使貢方物，謝前罪。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, the eunuch Zheng He visited their state; the king sent envoys offering local products and apologizing for his earlier offenses.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, Zheng He visited the kingdom. The king sent envoys with local products to apologize for his earlier misconduct.

sentences.zh: 七年，使來祭仁孝皇后，命中官告之几筵。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, envoys came to sacrifice to Empress Renxiao; eunuchs were ordered to announce this at the spirit tablet.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, envoys came to offer sacrifice to Empress Renxiao. Eunuchs were sent to announce the rite at her spirit tablet.

sentences.zh: 時奸民何八觀等逃入暹羅，帝命使 者還告其主，毋納逋逃。

translations.literal: At the time the wicked commoners He Baguan and others had fled into Siam; the Emperor ordered the envoys, on their return, to tell their ruler not to harbor fugitives.
translations.idiomatic: Outlaws led by He Baguan had fled into Siam. The Emperor told the returning envoys to warn their king not to shelter fugitives.

sentences.zh: 其王即奉命遣使貢馬及方物，並送八觀等還，命張原齎敕 幣獎之。

translations.literal: The king immediately obeyed the command, sent envoys offering horses and local products, and also returned Baguan and the others; Zhang Yuan was ordered to carry an imperial letter and silks to reward him.
translations.idiomatic: The king obeyed at once, sent horses and local products, and returned Baguan and his companions. Zhang Yuan was dispatched with an imperial letter and silks to reward him.

sentences.zh: 十年命中官洪保等往賜幣。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, eunuchs including Hong Bao were sent to bestow silks.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year, eunuchs led by Hong Bao were sent with silks as gifts.

sentences.zh: 十四年，王子三賴波羅摩剌答刂的賴遣使告父之喪。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, Prince Sanlai Boluomo La Dechode Lai sent envoys to report his father's death.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year, Prince Sanlai Borommaracha Decho De Lai sent envoys with news of his father's death.

sentences.zh: 命中官郭文往祭，別遣官 齎詔封其子為王，賜以素錦、素羅，隨遣使謝恩。

translations.literal: The eunuch Guo Wen was ordered to go and perform the mourning rites; separately officials were dispatched carrying an edict to enfeoff his son as king, granting plain brocades and plain gauze; envoys were sent along to express gratitude.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuch Guo Wen was sent to perform mourning rites, and other officials bore an edict investing the son as king with gifts of plain brocades and gauze. Envoys accompanied them to give thanks.

sentences.zh: 十七年命中官楊敏等護歸。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, eunuchs including Yang Min were ordered to escort them home.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year, eunuchs led by Yang Min escorted the envoys home.

sentences.zh: 以暹 羅侵滿剌加，遣使責令輯睦，王復遣使謝罪。

translations.literal: Because Siam had encroached upon Malacca, envoys were sent to rebuke it and order reconciliation; the king again sent envoys to apologize.
translations.idiomatic: When Siam encroached on Malacca, the court sent envoys to rebuke the kingdom and demand peace. The king sent envoys to apologize again.

sentences.zh: 宣德八年，王悉裡麻哈賴遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Xuande, King Xilimahalai sent envoys to pay court tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuande 8, King Xilimahalai sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 初，其國陪臣柰三鐸等貢舟次占城新州港，盡為其國人所掠。

translations.literal: Earlier, the attendant minister Nai Sanduo and others, when their tribute ship stopped at Champa's Xinzho Harbor, were entirely plundered by people of that state.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the attendant minister Nai Sanduo and his party had anchored at Champa's Xinzho Harbor, where Champa men plundered them completely.

sentences.zh: 正統元年，柰三 鐸潛附小舟來京，訴占城劫掠狀。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhengtong, Nai Sanduo secretly boarded a small boat and came to the capital, reporting the circumstances of Champa's robbery and plunder.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengtong 1, Nai Sanduo slipped aboard a small boat to the capital and petitioned about Champa's raid.

sentences.zh: 帝命召占城使者與相質。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Champa's envoys summoned to confront them in inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor summoned Champa's envoys to confront the accusers.

sentences.zh: 使者無以對，乃敕占城 王，令盡還所掠人物。

translations.literal: The envoys had nothing to answer; an edict was then issued to the king of Champa ordering the full return of all persons and goods plundered.
translations.idiomatic: The Champa envoys could not reply. The Emperor ordered the king of Champa to return every person and item taken.

sentences.zh: 已，占城移咨禮部言：「本國前歲遣使往須文達那，亦為暹 羅賊人掠去，必暹羅先還所掠，本國不敢不還。」

translations.literal: Soon afterward, Champa sent a communication to the Ministry of Rites saying: "Our state the year before last dispatched envoys to Xuwendana; they too were seized by Siam bandits. Siam must first return what it plundered; only then dare our state fail to return what it took."
translations.idiomatic: Champa then wrote the Ministry of Rites: "Two years ago our envoys bound for Xuwendana were also seized by Siam raiders. Siam must return its plunder first; only then can we return what we took."

sentences.zh: 三年，暹羅貢使又至，賜敕曉以 此意，令亟還占城人物。

translations.literal: In the third year, Siam's tribute envoys came again; an imperial letter was bestowed explaining this intent and ordering the swift return of Champa's people and goods.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, when Siam's envoys arrived again, the court sent an edict explaining this and demanding the immediate return of Champa's captives and goods.

sentences.zh: 十一年，王思利波羅麻那惹智剌遣使入貢。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, King Siluoboluo Manarezhila sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year, King Siluoboluo Manarezhila sent tribute envoys.

sentences.zh: 景泰四年，命給事中劉洙、行人劉泰祭其故王波羅摩剌答刂的賴，封其嗣子把 羅蘭米孫剌為王。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jingtai, Supervising Secretary Liu Zhu and Attendant Liu Tai were ordered to perform mourning rites for the late king Borommaracha Decho De Lai and to enfeoff his heir Ba Luolan Mi Sun La as king.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingtai 4, Liu Zhu of the Secretariat and Liu Tai were sent to mourn the late King Borommaracha Decho De Lai and invest his heir Ba Luolan Mi Sun La as king.

sentences.zh: 天順元年賜其貢使钑花金帶。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianshun, its tribute envoys were granted inlaid gold belts.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianshun 1, its tribute envoys received inlaid gold belts.

sentences.zh: 六年，王孛剌藍羅者直波智遣使朝 貢。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, King Bolalanluo Zhezhibozhi sent envoys to pay court tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, King Bolalanluo Zhezhibozhi sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 成化九年，貢使言天順元年所頒勘合，為蟲所蝕，乞改給，從之。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Chenghua, tribute envoys reported that the tally documents issued in the first year of Tianshun had been eaten by insects and requested replacements; the request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: In Chenghua 9, envoys reported that their Tianshun tally documents had been destroyed by insects and asked for new ones. The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 十七年，貢 使還，至中途竊買子女，且多載私鹽，命遣官戒諭諸番。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, as the tribute envoys were returning, midway they secretly bought children and also carried much private salt; an order was issued to dispatch officials to admonish the various foreign states.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year, returning envoys were found midway to have secretly bought children and carried large amounts of contraband salt. Officials were sent to warn all the foreign states.

sentences.zh: 先是，汀州人謝文彬，以 販鹽下海，飄入其國，仕至坤岳，猶天朝學士也。

translations.literal: Earlier, Xie Wenbin of Tingzhou, having gone to sea selling salt, drifted into their state, rose in office to Kun Yue—still like a Hanlin scholar of the Celestial Court.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Xie Wenbin of Tingzhou had gone to sea as a salt smuggler, been blown to Siam, and risen to the post of Kun Yue—a rank comparable to a Hanlin scholar at court.

sentences.zh: 後充使來朝，貿易禁物，事覺下 吏。

translations.literal: Later, serving as envoy on a mission to court, he traded in prohibited goods; when the matter came to light he was handed over to the judicial officials.
translations.idiomatic: Later, while serving as an envoy to court, he traded in banned goods. When discovered, he was turned over to the magistrates.

sentences.zh: 十八年遣使朝貢，且告父喪，命給事中林霄、行人姚隆往封其子國隆勃剌略坤 息剌尤地為王。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year envoys were sent to pay court tribute and report the father's death; Supervising Secretary Lin Xiao and Attendant Yao Long were ordered to go and enfeoff his son Guo Long Bo La Lue Kun Xi La You Di as king.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year, envoys came with tribute and news of the king's death. Lin Xiao and Yao Long were sent to invest the son Guo Long Bo La Lue Kun Xi La You Di as king.

sentences.zh: 弘治十年入貢。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Hongzhi, tribute was sent.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongzhi 10, the kingdom sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 時四夷館無暹羅譯字官，閣臣徐溥等請移牒廣東， 訪取能通彼國言語文字者，赴京備用，從之。

translations.literal: At the time the Four Barbarians Hall had no Siam translation clerk; Grand Secretaries Xu Pu and others requested that a notice be sent to Guangdong to seek out persons who could understand that state's language and script and send them to the capital for reserve duty; the request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The Four Barbarians Hall had no Siam interpreter. Grand Secretaries Xu Pu and others asked that Guangdong be instructed to find men fluent in Siam's language and script and send them to the capital. The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 正德四年，暹羅船有飄至廣東者，市 舶中官熊宣與守臣議，稅其物供軍需。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhengde, when Siam ships drifted to Guangdong, the maritime trade eunuch Xiong Xuan consulted with the defending officials and proposed taxing their goods to supply military needs.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengde 4, when Siam vessels were driven to Guangdong, maritime trade eunuch Xiong Xuan and local officials proposed taxing their cargo for military supplies.

sentences.zh: 事聞，詔斥宣妄攬事柄，撤還南京。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, an edict rebuked Xuan for presumptuously seizing authority and recalled him to Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the throne, an edict rebuked Xuan for overstepping his authority and recalled him to Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 十年進 金葉表朝貢，館中無識其字者。

translations.literal: In the tenth year they came with a gold-leaf memorial to pay court tribute, but in the hostel no one could read the script.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year they arrived with a gold-leaf memorial, but no one at the translation hostel could read their writing.

sentences.zh: 閣臣梁儲等請選留其使一二人入館肄習，報可。

translations.literal: Grand Secretaries Liang Chu and others requested that one or two of their envoys be selected and retained to study in the hostel; approval was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretaries Liang Chu and others asked that one or two envoys be kept to train at the hostel. The court approved.

sentences.zh: 嘉 靖元年，暹羅、占城貨船至廣東。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiajing, Siam and Champa merchant ships arrived at Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 1, merchant ships from Siam and Champa reached Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 市舶中官牛榮縱家人私市，論死如律。

translations.literal: The maritime trade eunuch Niu Rong allowed his household members to engage in private trade; he was sentenced to death according to the law.
translations.idiomatic: Maritime trade eunuch Niu Rong had let his household trade on the side; he was condemned to death under the statutes.

sentences.zh: 三十二年 遣使貢白象及方物，象死於途，使者以珠寶飾其牙，盛以金盤，並尾來獻。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year envoys were dispatched offering a white elephant and local products; the elephant died en route, and the envoys adorned its tusks with jewels, placed them in a gold dish, and also brought the tail to present.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-second year they sent envoys with a white elephant and local goods. The elephant died on the journey, so the envoys set its tusks with jewels, placed them in a gold dish, and brought the tail as well.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉其 意，厚遣之。

translations.literal: The Emperor approved their intent and sent them away with generous gifts.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor admired their thoughtfulness and rewarded them generously on their departure.

sentences.zh: 隆慶中，其鄰國東蠻牛求婚不得，慚怒，大發兵攻破其國。

translations.literal: During the Longqing reign, the neighboring state of Dongmanniu, having failed in a marriage proposal, was shamed and enraged, and raised a great army that broke through and conquered the kingdom.
translations.idiomatic: During Longqing, the neighboring realm of Dongmanniu, rebuffed in a marriage suit, flew into a rage and marched a great army that smashed the kingdom.

sentences.zh: 王自經，擄其世子 及天朝所賜印以歸。

translations.literal: The king hanged himself; they seized the crown prince and the seal bestowed by the Celestial Court and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: The king took his own life. The invaders carried off the crown prince and the seal the Celestial Court had granted, then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 次子嗣位，奉表請印，予之。

translations.literal: The second son succeeded to the throne, presented a memorial requesting a seal, and one was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The second son took the throne, petitioned for a new seal, and received one.

sentences.zh: 自是為東蠻牛所制，嗣王勵志復 仇。

translations.literal: From this time they were controlled by Dongmanniu; the succeeding king resolved to avenge the wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter they fell under Dongmanniu's sway, and the new king set his heart on revenge.

sentences.zh: 萬曆間，敵兵復至，王整兵奮擊，大破之，殺其子，餘眾宵遁，暹羅由是雄海 上。

translations.literal: During the Wanli reign enemy troops came again; the king marshaled his forces and fought fiercely, routing them completely, killing the enemy's son; the remainder fled by night, and Siam from this became dominant on the seas.
translations.idiomatic: In the Wanli era the enemy returned. The king rallied his troops, struck hard, and routed them, killing the invader's son while the rest fled under cover of night. From that point Siam dominated the seas.

sentences.zh: 移兵攻破真臘，降其王。

translations.literal: He shifted his army, broke through and conquered Khmer, and reduced its king to submission.
translations.idiomatic: He turned his armies against Khmer, broke the kingdom, and forced its king to submit.

sentences.zh: 從此歲歲用兵，遂霸諸國。

translations.literal: From this time he waged war year after year and thus came to dominate the various states.
translations.idiomatic: He campaigned every year thereafter and came to lord it over the surrounding kingdoms.

sentences.zh: 六年遣使入貢。

translations.literal: In the sixth year envoys were sent with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year the kingdom sent tribute envoys.

sentences.zh: 二十年，日本破朝鮮，暹羅請潛師直搗日本，牽其後。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, when Japan broke Korea, Siam requested to send a secret force straight against Japan to strike at its rear.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year, after Japan overran Korea, Siam offered to send a covert force against Japan's rear.

sentences.zh: 中樞石 星議從之，兩廣督臣蕭彥持不可，乃已。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Shi Xing of the Secretariat argued in favor; the Guangdong-Guangxi governor-general Xiao Yan objected that it could not be done, and the plan was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Shi Xing favored the plan, but Governor-General Xiao Yan of the Two Guangs opposed it, and the matter was dropped.

sentences.zh: 其後，奉貢不替。

translations.literal: Afterward, tribute missions continued without interruption.
translations.idiomatic: Tribute missions continued without fail thereafter.

sentences.zh: 崇禎十六年猶入貢。

translations.literal: Even in the sixteenth year of Chongzhen tribute still came.
translations.idiomatic: As late as Chongzhen 16 the kingdom still sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 其國，周千里，風俗勁悍，習於水戰。

translations.literal: The state measures a thousand li in circumference; its customs are fierce and hardy, and its people are practiced in naval warfare.
translations.idiomatic: The kingdom spans a thousand li in circuit. Its people are fierce and hardy, skilled in fighting at sea.

sentences.zh: 大將用聖鐵裹身，刀矢不能入。

translations.literal: Great generals wrap their bodies in sacred iron, and neither blades nor arrows can pierce them.
translations.idiomatic: Senior commanders arm themselves in sacred iron, proof against blade and arrow alike.

sentences.zh: 聖鐵者， 人腦骨也。

translations.literal: Sacred iron is human skull bone.
translations.idiomatic: Sacred iron is made from human skull bone.

sentences.zh: 王，瑣裡人。

translations.literal: The king is a man of Semudera.
translations.idiomatic: The king is of Semudera stock.

sentences.zh: 官分十等。

translations.literal: Official ranks are divided into ten grades.
translations.idiomatic: Official ranks fall into ten grades.

sentences.zh: 自王至庶民，有事皆決於其婦。

translations.literal: From the king down to commoners, whenever there is business it is all decided by their wives.
translations.idiomatic: From king to commoner, every matter of consequence is decided by the wife.

sentences.zh: 其婦人志量， 實出男子上。

translations.literal: The resolve and capacity of their women truly surpass those of men.
translations.idiomatic: Their women possess judgment and force of will that outmatch the men.

sentences.zh: 婦私華人，則夫置酒同飲，恬不為怪，曰：「我婦美，而為華人所悅 也。」

translations.literal: If a wife takes a Chinese lover, the husband sets out wine and drinks with them, untroubled and unperturbed, saying: "My wife is beautiful, and Chinese men are pleased with her."
translations.idiomatic: If a wife takes a Chinese lover, the husband will set out wine and drink with them without a qualm, saying, "My wife is beautiful, and Chinese men admire her."

sentences.zh: 崇信釋教，男女多為僧尼，亦居菴寺，持齋受戒。

translations.literal: They revere Buddhism; many men and women become monks and nuns, also dwelling in temples, keeping the fast and receiving precepts.
translations.idiomatic: They are devout Buddhists. Many men and women become monks and nuns, live in temples, and keep fasts and vows.

sentences.zh: 衣服頗類中國。

translations.literal: Their clothing is quite similar to China's.
translations.idiomatic: Their dress resembles that of China.

sentences.zh: 富貴者， 尤敬佛，百金之產，即以其半施之。

translations.literal: The wealthy, especially, revere the Buddha; of an estate worth a hundred pieces of gold, half is given away in offerings.
translations.idiomatic: The wealthy are especially devout: half of a fortune of a hundred gold pieces goes to the Buddha.

sentences.zh: 氣候不正，或寒或熱，地卑濕，人皆樓居。

translations.literal: The climate is irregular, sometimes cold and sometimes hot; the land is low and damp, and all live in raised houses.
translations.idiomatic: The climate swings erratically between cold and heat. The land is low and wet, and everyone lives in stilt houses.

sentences.zh: 男 女椎結，以白布裹首。

translations.literal: Men and women wear their hair in topknots and wrap their heads in white cloth.
translations.idiomatic: Men and women wear topknots and wrap their heads in white cloth.

sentences.zh: 富貴者死，用水銀灌其口而葬之。

translations.literal: When the wealthy die, mercury is poured into the mouth and they are buried.
translations.idiomatic: When the wealthy die, mercury is poured into the mouth before burial.

sentences.zh: 貧者則移置海濱，即有群 鴉飛啄，俄頃而盡，家人拾其骨號泣而棄之於海，謂之鳥葬。

translations.literal: The poor are moved and placed on the seashore; at once flocks of crows fly down to peck, and in a moment nothing remains; the family gathers the bones, wailing, and casts them into the sea—this is called bird burial.
translations.idiomatic: The poor are laid out on the shore. Crows descend at once and pick the body clean in moments. The family gathers the bones, weeping, and casts them into the sea. This is called bird burial.

sentences.zh: 亦延僧設齋禮佛。

translations.literal: They also invite monks to set out vegetarian feasts and worship the Buddha.
translations.idiomatic: Monks are invited to hold vegetarian rites and worship the Buddha as well.

sentences.zh: 交 易用海。

translations.literal: Trade uses cowrie shells.
translations.idiomatic: Cowrie shells serve as currency in trade.

sentences.zh: 是年不用，則國必大疫。

translations.literal: If they are not used that year, the state will surely suffer a great pestilence.
translations.idiomatic: If cowries are not used in a given year, the kingdom will surely suffer a great plague.

sentences.zh: 其貢物，有像、象牙、犀角、孔雀尾、翠羽、龜 筒、六足龜、寶石、珊瑚、片腦、米腦、糠腦、腦油、腦柴、薔薇水、碗石、丁皮、 阿魏、紫梗、藤竭、藤黃、硫黃、沒藥、烏爹泥、安息香、羅斛香、速香、檀香、 黃熟香、降真香、乳香、樹香、木香、丁香、烏香、胡椒、蘇木、肉荳蔻、白荳蔻、 蓽茇、烏木、大楓子及撒哈剌、西洋諸布。

translations.literal: Their tribute goods include images, ivory, rhinoceros horn, peacock tails, kingfisher feathers, tortoise shells, six-legged tortoises, precious stones, coral, camphor flakes, rice camphor, bran camphor, camphor oil, camphor wood, rosewater, bowl stones, cassia bark, asafetida, purple stem, rattan gum, gamboge, sulfur, myrrh, bismuth ocher, benzoin, lohu incense, gharuwood, sandalwood, aged sandalwood, eaglewood, frankincense, tree resin, costus, cloves, aloeswood, pepper, sappanwood, nutmeg, cardamom, long pepper, ebony, galangal seeds, and Sahala and various Western Ocean cloths.
translations.idiomatic: Their tribute includes images, ivory, rhinoceros horn, peacock tails, kingfisher feathers, tortoise shells, six-legged tortoises, gems, coral, camphor in many forms, rosewater, bowl stones, cassia, asafetida, gamboge, sulfur, myrrh, bismuth ocher, benzoin, and a long list of aromatics—lohu, gharuwood, sandalwood, eaglewood, frankincense, cloves, pepper, sappanwood, nutmeg, cardamom, long pepper, ebony, galangal seeds—along with Sahala and other Western Ocean cloths.

sentences.zh: 其國有三寶廟，祀中官鄭和。

translations.literal: The state has three Sanbao temples enshrining the eunuch Zheng He.
translations.idiomatic: The kingdom maintains three Sanbao temples dedicated to the eunuch Zheng He.

sentences.zh: 爪哇在占城西南。

translations.literal: Java lies southwest of Champa.
translations.idiomatic: Java lies to the southwest of Champa.

sentences.zh: 元世祖時，遣使臣孟琪往，黥其面。

translations.literal: During the time of Kublai Khan, an envoy named Meng Qi was sent there and had his face tattooed as punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Under Kublai Khan, the envoy Meng Qi was sent there and had his face branded in punishment.

sentences.zh: 世祖大舉兵伐之，破其 國而還。

translations.literal: The Khan raised a great army to attack it, broke the state, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The Khan marched a great army against it, broke the kingdom, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 洪武二年，太祖遣使以即位詔諭其國。

translations.literal: In the second year of Hongwu, the Founding Emperor dispatched envoys bearing an accession edict to announce instructions to the state.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 2, the Founding Emperor sent envoys with an accession edict to the kingdom.

sentences.zh: 其使臣先奉貢於元，還至福建而元亡， 因入居京師。

translations.literal: Its envoys had first offered tribute to the Yuan; on their return they reached Fujian just as the Yuan fell, and so they entered and took up residence in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Its envoys had been paying tribute to the Yuan. Returning, they reached Fujian as the dynasty collapsed and settled in the capital instead.

sentences.zh: 太祖復遣使送之還，且賜以《大統歷》。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor again dispatched envoys to escort them home and also bestowed the Datong Calendar.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor sent envoys to escort them home and granted them the Datong Calendar.

sentences.zh: 三年以平定沙漠頒詔曰： 「自古為天下主者，視天地所覆載，日月所照臨，若遠若近，生人之類，莫不欲其 安土而樂生。

translations.literal: In the third year, upon pacifying the desert, an edict was promulgated, saying: "Since antiquity, whoever holds lordship over the realm looks upon all that Heaven and Earth cover and bear, all that sun and moon shine upon, near and far alike; among the classes of living people, none do not desire to settle on their own soil and live in contentment.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, after pacifying the desert, an edict proclaimed: "Since antiquity, the ruler of the realm has looked upon all Heaven and Earth uphold, all sun and moon illuminate, near and far alike. Every living people wishes to dwell in peace on its own soil.

sentences.zh: 然必中國安，而後四方萬國順附。

translations.literal: Yet China must first be secure, and only then will the myriad states of the four quarters submit in obedience.
translations.idiomatic: But China must be secure first; only then will the myriad states of the four quarters submit.

sentences.zh: 邇元君妥懽帖木兒，荒淫昏弱，志 不在民。

translations.literal: Recently the Yuan ruler Toghon Temür was dissolute, debauched, and feeble; his mind was not set upon the people.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuan ruler Toghon Temür was dissolute, weak, and indifferent to his people.

sentences.zh: 天下英雄，分裂疆宇。

translations.literal: Heroes throughout the realm split the territory apart.
translations.idiomatic: Heroes across the realm carved up the land.

sentences.zh: 朕憫生民之塗炭，興舉義兵，攘除亂略。

translations.literal: I took pity on the people in their misery, raised righteous troops, and swept away disorder and violence.
translations.idiomatic: I took pity on the people in their misery, raised righteous armies, and swept away chaos and violence.

sentences.zh: 天下軍民 共尊朕居帝位，國號大明，建元洪武。

translations.literal: The armies and people of the realm together honored me with the imperial throne; the state is styled Great Ming, and the reign era is Hongwu.
translations.idiomatic: The armies and people of the realm together raised me to the throne. The dynasty is called Great Ming, and the reign era Hongwu.

sentences.zh: 前年克取元都，四方底定。

translations.literal: The year before last we captured the Yuan capital, and the four quarters were settled.
translations.idiomatic: Two years ago we took the Yuan capital, and the four quarters were settled.

sentences.zh: 占城、安南、高 麗諸國，俱來朝貢。

translations.literal: Champa, Annam, Goryeo, and other states all came to court with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Champa, Annam, Goryeo, and other kingdoms all came to court with tribute.

sentences.zh: 今年遣將北征，始知元君已沒，獲其孫買的裡八刺，封為崇禮 侯。

translations.literal: This year, dispatching generals on a northern campaign, we learned that the Yuan ruler had died; we captured his grandson Buyidili Baci and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Chongli.
translations.idiomatic: This year our northern campaign learned that the Yuan ruler was dead. We captured his grandson Buyidili Baci and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Chongli.

sentences.zh: 朕仿前代帝王，治理天下，惟欲中外人民，各安其所。

translations.literal: I follow the emperors of former ages in governing the realm, desiring only that the people within and without each dwell in their proper places.
translations.idiomatic: I govern as emperors of old did, wishing only that people within and beyond the realm may each live in peace where they belong.

sentences.zh: 又慮諸蕃僻在遠方，未 悉朕意，故遣使者往諭，咸使聞知。」

translations.literal: I also feared that the various foreign states, remote in distant regions, might not fully understand my intent, and therefore dispatched envoys to announce instructions, so that all might hear and know."
translations.idiomatic: Fearing that distant foreign states might not understand my intent, I have sent envoys to proclaim it so that all may know."

sentences.zh: 九月，其王昔裡八達剌蒲遣使奉金葉表來朝， 貢方物，宴賚如禮。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, King Xilbidalabu sent envoys presenting a gold-leaf memorial to attend court, offered local products, and was feasted and rewarded according to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, King Xilbidalabu sent envoys with a gold-leaf memorial and local products. They were feasted and rewarded according to ritual.

sentences.zh: 五年又遣使隨朝使常克敬來貢，上元所授宣敕三道。

translations.literal: In the fifth year envoys were again sent, following the court envoy Chang Kejing, to offer tribute, presenting three Yuan patents and edicts.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year envoys came again with court envoy Chang Kejing, bearing tribute and three patents and edicts granted by the Yuan.

sentences.zh: 八年又貢。

translations.literal: In the eighth year tribute came again.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year they sent tribute again.

sentences.zh: 十年，王八達 那巴那務遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, King Badanabanawu sent envoys to pay court tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year, King Badanabanawu sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 其國又有東、西二王，東蕃王勿院勞網結，西蕃王勿勞波務， 各遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: The state also had eastern and western kings: the Eastern king Wuyuanlaowangjie and the Western king Wulaobowu each sent envoys to pay court tribute.
translations.idiomatic: The kingdom also had eastern and western kings. The Eastern king Wuyuanlaowangjie and the Western king Wulaobowu each sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 天子以其禮意不誠，詔留其使，已而釋還之。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven, finding their ritual intent insincere, ordered their envoys detained; soon afterward they were released and sent back.
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven found their courtesy insincere and ordered their envoys detained, then released and sent home.

sentences.zh: 十二年，王八達那巴那 務遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, King Badanabanawu sent envoys to pay court tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year, King Badanabanawu sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 明年又貢。

translations.literal: The next year tribute came again.
translations.idiomatic: The following year they sent tribute again.

sentences.zh: 時遣使賜三佛齊王印綬，爪哇誘而殺之。

translations.literal: At the time envoys were dispatched to bestow a seal and cord upon the king of Srivijaya; Java lured and killed them.
translations.idiomatic: At that time envoys were sent to invest the king of Srivijaya with seal and cord. Java lured them in and killed them.

sentences.zh: 天子怒，留其使 月餘，將加罪，已，遣還，賜敕責之。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven was enraged, detained their envoys for more than a month, and was about to punish them; soon afterward he sent them back, bestowing an imperial rebuke.
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven was furious. He held Java's envoys for more than a month and was about to punish them, then sent them home with a stern rebuke.
