sentences.zh: 十四年遣使貢黑奴三百人及他方物。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year envoys were sent offering three hundred black slaves and other local products.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year they sent three hundred black slaves and other local goods as tribute.

sentences.zh: 明年又 貢黑奴男女百人、大珠八顆、胡椒七萬五千斤。

translations.literal: The next year they again offered one hundred black slaves, male and female, eight large pearls, and seventy-five thousand jin of pepper.
translations.idiomatic: The next year they sent one hundred black slaves, eight large pearls, and seventy-five thousand jin of pepper.

sentences.zh: 二十六年再貢。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year tribute came again.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year they sent tribute once more.

sentences.zh: 明年又貢。

translations.literal: The next year tribute came again.
translations.idiomatic: The following year they sent tribute again.

sentences.zh: 成祖即位，詔諭其國。

translations.literal: When the Yongle Emperor ascended the throne, he issued an edict to instruct their state.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yongle Emperor took the throne, he sent an edict to their country.

sentences.zh: 永樂元年又遣副使聞良輔、行人甯善，賜其王絨、綿、 織金文綺、紗羅。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongle, Vice Envoy Wen Liangfu and Attendant Ning Shan were again dispatched to bestow upon the king velvet, cotton, brocaded silks, and gauze.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle 1, Vice Envoy Wen Liangfu and Attendant Ning Shan were sent with velvet, cotton, brocaded silks, and gauze for the king.

sentences.zh: 使者既行，其西王都馬板遣使入賀，覆命中官馬彬等賜以鍍金銀 印。

translations.literal: After the envoys had departed, the Western king Duma Ban sent envoys to offer congratulations; eunuchs including Ma Bin were again ordered to bestow a gilded silver seal.
translations.idiomatic: After those envoys had left, the Western king Duma Ban sent envoys to offer congratulations. Eunuchs led by Ma Bin were again ordered to grant a gilded silver seal.

sentences.zh: 西王遣使謝賜印，貢方物。

translations.literal: The Western king sent envoys to thank him for the bestowed seal and offered local products.
translations.idiomatic: The Western king sent envoys to thank the court for the seal and brought local products.

sentences.zh: 而東王孛令達哈亦遣使朝貢，請印，命遣官賜之。

translations.literal: The Eastern king Boling Daha also sent envoys to pay court tribute and requested a seal; an order was issued to dispatch officials to bestow one.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern king Boling Daha also sent envoys with tribute and asked for a seal. Officials were ordered to grant one.

sentences.zh: 自後，二王並貢。

translations.literal: From this time both kings sent tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter both kings sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 三年遣中官鄭和使其國。

translations.literal: In the third year the eunuch Zheng He was dispatched on a mission to their state.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year the eunuch Zheng He was sent on a mission to the kingdom.

sentences.zh: 明年，西王與東王構兵，東王戰敗，國被滅。

translations.literal: The next year the Western king and Eastern king raised arms against each other; the Eastern king was defeated in battle and his state was destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the Western and Eastern kings went to war. The Eastern king was defeated and his realm destroyed.

sentences.zh: 適朝使 經東王地，部卒入市，西王國人殺之，凡百七十人。

translations.literal: Just then court envoys were passing through Eastern king territory; escort soldiers entered the market, and men of the Western king's state killed them—one hundred seventy in all.
translations.idiomatic: Court envoys happened to be passing through Eastern king territory. Escort soldiers entered the market, and Western king's men killed them—one hundred seventy in all.

sentences.zh: 西王懼，遣使謝罪。

translations.literal: The Western king was afraid and sent envoys to apologize.
translations.idiomatic: The Western king was terrified and sent envoys to apologize.

sentences.zh: 帝賜敕切 責之，命輸黃金六萬兩以贖。

translations.literal: The Emperor bestowed an imperial letter sternly rebuking him and ordered payment of sixty thousand taels of gold as ransom.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sent a stern rebuke and ordered payment of sixty thousand taels of gold as ransom.

sentences.zh: 六年再遣鄭和使其國。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Zheng He was again dispatched on a mission to their state.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Zheng He was sent to the kingdom again.

sentences.zh: 西王獻黃金萬兩，禮官以輸數 不足，請下其使於獄。

translations.literal: The Western king offered ten thousand taels of gold; the ritual officials, finding the amount paid insufficient, requested that his envoys be placed in prison.
translations.idiomatic: The Western king offered ten thousand taels of gold. Ritual officials found the sum short and asked that his envoys be imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朕於遠人，欲其畏罪而已，寧利其金耶？」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Toward distant peoples, I wish only that they fear guilt—would I profit from their gold?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "With distant peoples I want only that they fear wrongdoing. Would I profit from their gold?"

sentences.zh: 悉捐之。

translations.literal: He remitted it all.
translations.idiomatic: He remitted the entire sum.

sentences.zh: 自後，比年一貢，或間歲一貢，或一歲數貢。

translations.literal: From this time tribute came every other year, or every few years, or several times in one year.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter tribute came every other year, every few years, or several times in a single year.

sentences.zh: 中官吳賓、鄭和先後使其國。

translations.literal: The eunuchs Wu Bin and Zheng He successively served as envoys to their state.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs Wu Bin and Zheng He visited the kingdom in turn.

sentences.zh: 時舊港 地有為爪哇侵據者，滿剌加國王矯朝命索之。

translations.literal: At the time there were places in Old Port territory occupied by Java; the king of Malacca, falsely invoking a court command, demanded them back.
translations.idiomatic: Old Port lands had been seized by Java. The king of Malacca, falsely claiming a court order, demanded them back.

sentences.zh: 帝乃賜敕曰：「前中官尹慶還，言王 恭待敕使，有加無替。

translations.literal: The Emperor then bestowed an imperial letter, saying: "When the eunuch Yin Qing returned earlier, he reported that the king received imperial envoys with respect, treating them ever more generously.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor then sent an edict: "When eunuch Yin Qing returned earlier, he reported that you received imperial envoys with growing courtesy.

sentences.zh: 比聞滿剌加國索舊港之地，王甚疑懼。

translations.literal: I have lately heard that Malacca is demanding Old Port territory, and the king is greatly suspicious and afraid.
translations.idiomatic: I have lately heard that Malacca is demanding Old Port territory, and you are greatly alarmed.

sentences.zh: 朕推誠待人，若果許 之，必有敕諭，王何疑焉。

translations.literal: I treat people with sincere good faith; if such a thing were truly granted, there would surely be an imperial instruction—why should the king doubt?
translations.idiomatic: I deal with others in good faith. If I truly granted such a demand, you would receive an imperial instruction. Why doubt?

sentences.zh: 小人浮詞，慎勿輕聽。」

translations.literal: Do not lightly heed the empty words of petty men."
translations.idiomatic: Do not lightly heed the gossip of petty men."

sentences.zh: 十三年，其王改名揚惟西沙， 遣使謝恩，貢方物。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, the king changed his name to Yang Weixisha, sent envoys to express gratitude, and offered local products.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year the king took the name Yang Weixisha and sent envoys with thanks and local products.

sentences.zh: 時朝使所攜卒有遭風飄至班卒兒國者，爪哇人珍班聞之，用金 贖還，歸之王所。

translations.literal: At the time some soldiers accompanying court envoys were blown by wind to the state of Pancur; the Java man Zhen Ban heard of it, used gold to ransom them back, and returned them to the king's court.
translations.idiomatic: Some soldiers with court envoys were blown off course to Pancur. A Java man named Zhen Ban heard of it, ransomed them with gold, and returned them to the king.

sentences.zh: 十六年，王遣使朝貢，因送還諸卒。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year the king sent envoys to pay court tribute and also returned the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year the king sent envoys with tribute and returned the soldiers.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉之，賜敕獎王，並優賜 珍班。

translations.literal: The Emperor approved, bestowed an imperial letter commending the king, and also granted Zhen Ban special rewards.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor commended the king with an imperial letter and rewarded Zhen Ban generously as well.

sentences.zh: 自是，朝貢使臣大率每歲一至。

translations.literal: From this time tribute envoys generally came once each year.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter tribute envoys generally came about once a year.

sentences.zh: 正統元年，使臣馬用良言：「先任八諦來朝，蒙恩賜銀帶。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhengtong, envoy Ma Yongliang said: "The former officeholder Badhi came to court and received the grace of a silver belt.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengtong 1, envoy Ma Yongliang said: "The former officeholder Badhi came to court and was granted a silver belt.

sentences.zh: 今為亞烈，秩四品，乞賜金帶。」

translations.literal: I now hold the office of Yale, rank fourth grade, and beg that a gold belt be granted."
translations.idiomatic: I now hold the office of Yale at fourth rank and beg for a gold belt."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 閏六月遣古裡、蘇門答剌、錫蘭山、柯枝、天方、加異勒、阿丹、忽魯謨斯、祖法兒、甘巴裡、真臘使臣偕爪哇使臣郭信等同往。

translations.literal: In the intercalary sixth month envoys from Calicut, Samudra, Ceylon, Cochin, Tianfang, Kayal, Aden, Hormuz, Dhofar, Cambay, and Chenla were sent together with Java envoy Guo Xin to return home.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary sixth month envoys from Calicut, Samudra, Ceylon, Cochin, Tianfang, Kayal, Aden, Hormuz, Dhofar, Cambay, and Chenla were sent home together with Java envoy Guo Xin.

sentences.zh: 賜爪哇敕曰：「王自我先朝，修職勿怠。

translations.literal: An edict was granted to Java, saying: "From my predecessor's reign you have kept your duties—do not slacken.
translations.idiomatic: An edict to Java said: "From my predecessor's reign you have kept your duties—do not slacken.

sentences.zh: 朕今嗣服，復遣使來朝，意誠具悉。

translations.literal: I have now succeeded to the throne, and you again send envoys to court; your sincere intent is fully understood.
translations.idiomatic: I have now succeeded to the throne, and you again send envoys to court; your sincerity is fully understood.

sentences.zh: 宣德時，有古裡等十一國來貢，今因王使者歸，令諸使同往。

translations.literal: During Xuande, Calicut and ten other states came with tribute; now, because your envoy is returning, I order the other envoys to go together with him.
translations.idiomatic: During Xuande, Calicut and ten other states sent tribute; now, as your envoy returns, I order the other envoys to go with him.

sentences.zh: 王其加意撫綏，分遣還國，副朕懷遠之忱。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty should take care to soothe and settle them, send them back to their countries, and fulfill my desire to cherish those afar."
translations.idiomatic: Take care to settle them and send them home, fulfilling my desire to cherish distant peoples."

sentences.zh: 五年，使臣回，遭風溺死五十六人，存者八十三人，仍返廣東。

translations.literal: In the fifth year the envoys returned; fifty-six were drowned in a storm, eighty-three survived, and they still came back to Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 the envoys returned; fifty-six drowned in a storm, eighty-three survived, and they reached Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 命所司廩給，俟便舟附歸。

translations.literal: The responsible offices were ordered to supply provisions and wait for a convenient vessel to send them home.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible offices were ordered to supply provisions and wait for a convenient ship to send them home.

sentences.zh: 八年，廣東參政張琰言：「爪哇朝貢頻數，供億費煩，敝中國以事遠人，非計。」

translations.literal: In the eighth year, Guangdong Vice Commissioner Zhang Yan reported: "Java's tribute missions come too frequently; the costs of provision and entertainment are burdensome. To exhaust China in serving distant peoples is no sound policy."
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, Guangdong Vice Commissioner Zhang Yan reported: "Java's tribute missions come too often. The cost of hosting them drains the empire. Exhausting China to serve distant realms is no sound policy."

sentences.zh: 帝納之。

translations.literal: The Emperor accepted the advice.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor accepted the advice.

sentences.zh: 其使還，賜敕曰：「海外諸邦，並三年一貢。

translations.literal: When their envoys returned, an imperial letter was bestowed, saying: "All overseas states shall send tribute once every three years.
translations.idiomatic: When their envoys returned, an edict declared: "All overseas states shall send tribute once every three years.

sentences.zh: 王亦宜體恤軍民，一遵此制。」

translations.literal: The king should also show concern for armies and people and strictly follow this regulation."
translations.idiomatic: The king should show concern for his armies and people and follow this rule."

sentences.zh: 十一年復三貢，後乃漸稀。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year tribute came three times again; afterward it gradually grew rare.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year they sent tribute three times again, but missions gradually grew rare thereafter.

sentences.zh: 景泰三年，王巴剌武遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jingtai, King Balawu sent envoys to pay court tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingtai 3, King Balawu sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 天順四年，王都馬班遣使入貢。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianshun, King Duma Ban sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianshun 4, King Duma Ban sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 使者還至安慶， 酗酒，與入貢番僧斗，僧死者六人。

translations.literal: When the envoys returned and reached Anqing, they drank to excess, fought with foreign monks who had come bearing tribute, and six monks died.
translations.idiomatic: On the return journey the envoys reached Anqing, got drunk, and brawled with tribute-bearing foreign monks; six monks were killed.

sentences.zh: 禮官請治伴送行人罪，使者敕國王自治，從之。

translations.literal: The ritual officials requested punishment for the accompanying escorts; an edict ordered the king to punish the envoys himself, and this was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Rites asked that the escorts be punished. The court ordered the king to discipline the envoys on his own, and this was approved.

sentences.zh: 成化元年入貢。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chenghua they sent tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In Chenghua 1 they sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 弘治十二年，貢使遭風舟壞，止通事一舟達廣東。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Hongzhi, the tribute envoys were struck by wind and their boats were wrecked; only the interpreter's single boat reached Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongzhi 12, the tribute mission was hit by a storm and the boats were lost; only the interpreter's boat reached Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 禮官請敕所司， 量予賜賚遣還，其貢物仍進京師，制可。

translations.literal: The ritual officials requested an edict to the relevant offices to grant appropriate gifts and send them back, while the tribute goods should still be forwarded to the capital; the order was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Rites asked that the relevant offices be ordered to give suitable gifts and send the envoys home, while the tribute goods should still go to the capital. The order was approved.

sentences.zh: 自是貢使鮮有至者。

translations.literal: From this time onward, tribute envoys rarely came.
translations.idiomatic: After that, tribute missions rarely arrived.

sentences.zh: 其國近占城，二十晝夜可至。

translations.literal: The state is near Champa; one can reach it in twenty day-and-night journeys.
translations.idiomatic: The kingdom lies close to Champa, about twenty days' sail away.

sentences.zh: 元師西征，以至元二十九年十二月發泉州，明年 正月即抵其國，相去止月餘。

translations.literal: On the Yuan army's western campaign, it departed Quanzhou in the twelfth month of the twenty-ninth year of Zhiyuan and reached that state in the first month of the following year—a span of little more than one month.
translations.idiomatic: On the Yuan western expedition, the army left Quanzhou in the twelfth month of Zhiyuan 29 and reached Java the following first month—barely more than a month apart.

sentences.zh: 宣德七年入貢，表書「一千三百七十六年」，蓋漢宣 帝元康元年，乃其建國之始也。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Xuande they sent tribute; their memorial gave the year "1376," which corresponds to the first year of Yuankang under Emperor Xuan of Han—the beginning of their state.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuande 7 they sent tribute. Their memorial dated the year to "1376," taken as the first year of Yuankang under Emperor Xuan of Han—the founding of their kingdom.

sentences.zh: 地廣人稠。

translations.literal: The land is broad and the population dense.
translations.idiomatic: The country is vast and densely populated.

sentences.zh: 性凶悍，男子無少長貴賤皆佩刀，稍忤 輒相賊，故其甲兵為諸蕃之最。

translations.literal: By nature they are fierce and violent; men of all ages and ranks wear swords at their waists, and the slightest offense leads them to kill one another, so their arms and soldiers are the greatest among all the foreign states.
translations.idiomatic: They are fierce by nature. Men of every age and rank go armed, and the least provocation turns to bloodshed, so their fighting men are the strongest among the foreign states.

sentences.zh: 字類瑣裡，無紙筆，刻於茭曌葉。

translations.literal: Their writing resembles that of Semudera; they have no paper or brush and inscribe on palm leaves.
translations.idiomatic: Their script resembles Semudera's. They use no paper or brush, carving their writing on palm leaves instead.

sentences.zh: 氣候常似夏，稻 歲二稔。

translations.literal: The climate is always like summer, and rice yields two harvests per year.
translations.idiomatic: The climate is perpetually summerlike, and rice is harvested twice a year.

sentences.zh: 無幾榻匕箸。

translations.literal: They have no tables, couches, spoons, or chopsticks.
translations.idiomatic: They use no tables, couches, spoons, or chopsticks.

sentences.zh: 人有三種：華人流寓者，服食鮮華；

translations.literal: There are three kinds of people: Chinese who have settled there dress and eat in fine style;
translations.idiomatic: The population falls into three groups: Chinese settlers, who dress and dine elegantly;

sentences.zh: 他國賈人居久者，亦尚 雅潔；

translations.literal: merchants of other states who have lived there long also value refinement and cleanliness;
translations.idiomatic: long-resident foreign merchants, who also favor refinement and cleanliness;

sentences.zh: 其本國人最污穢，好啖蛇蟻蟲蚓，與犬同寢食，狀黝黑，猱頭赤腳。

translations.literal: the native people of the state itself are the most filthy, fond of eating snakes, ants, insects, and earthworms, sleeping and eating with dogs, dark in appearance, with monkey-like heads and bare feet.
translations.idiomatic: and the natives themselves, the most unclean of all, who eat snakes, ants, insects, and earthworms, sleep and eat with dogs, and are dark-skinned, with shaggy heads and bare feet.

sentences.zh: 崇信鬼 道。

translations.literal: They revere the way of ghosts and spirits.
translations.idiomatic: They worship spirits and demons.

sentences.zh: 殺人者避之三日即免罪。

translations.literal: A killer who hides for three days is absolved of guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Murderers who remain in hiding for three days go unpunished.

sentences.zh: 父母死，舁至野，縱犬食之；

translations.literal: When parents die, the body is carried into the wild and dogs are set loose to eat it;
translations.idiomatic: When parents die, the body is taken into the wild and left for dogs;

sentences.zh: 不盡，則大戚，燔其餘。

translations.literal: if it is not fully consumed, they wail greatly and burn what remains.
translations.idiomatic: if the dogs do not finish it, they mourn bitterly and burn the rest.

sentences.zh: 妻妾多燔以殉。

translations.literal: Many wives and concubines are burned to follow the dead in death.
translations.idiomatic: Many wives and concubines are burned alive to accompany the dead.

sentences.zh: 其國一名莆家龍，又曰下港，曰順塔。

translations.literal: The state is also called Pujialong, also called Xiagang, and also called Shunta.
translations.idiomatic: The kingdom is also known as Pujialong, Xiagang, and Shunta.

sentences.zh: 萬曆時，紅毛番築土庫於大澗東，佛郎 機築於大澗西，歲歲互市。

translations.literal: In the Wanli era, the Red-Haired foreigners built earthen warehouses east of Da Jian, and the Franks built on the west; every year they traded with one another.
translations.idiomatic: During the Wanli reign, Dutch traders built warehouses east of Da Jian and the Portuguese on the west, and the two sides traded with each other every year.

sentences.zh: 中國商旅亦往來不絕。

translations.literal: Chinese merchants and travelers also came and went without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Chinese merchants traveled back and forth without interruption.

sentences.zh: 其國有新村，最號饒富。

translations.literal: The state has a place called New Village, renowned as the richest.
translations.idiomatic: The kingdom has a settlement called New Village, famed as the wealthiest.

sentences.zh: 中華及 諸番商舶，輻輳其地，寶貨填溢。

translations.literal: Chinese and foreign merchant ships converged on the place, and precious goods overflowed.
translations.idiomatic: Chinese and foreign merchant vessels crowded its harbor until treasures overflowed.

sentences.zh: 其村主即廣東人，永樂九年自遣使表貢方物。

translations.literal: The village chief was a man of Guangdong; in the ninth year of Yongle he himself sent envoys with a memorial and local products as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: The village head was a Guangdong man who, in Yongle 9, sent his own envoys with a memorial and tribute goods.

sentences.zh: 阇婆，古曰阇婆達。

translations.literal: Java, anciently called Jaraboda.
translations.idiomatic: Java was anciently known as Jaraboda.

sentences.zh: 宋元嘉時，始朝中國。

translations.literal: In the Yuanjia era of Liu Song, it first paid court to China.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Liu Song emperor Yuanjia, it first sent missions to the Chinese court.

sentences.zh: 唐曰訶陵，又曰社婆，其王居阇婆 城，宋曰阇婆，皆入貢。

translations.literal: Under Tang it was called Heling, also called Shepo; its king dwelt in Jaraboda city. Under Song it was called Java, and in all cases it sent tribute.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang knew it as Heling, also called Shepo, with its king at Jaraboda. The Song called it Java. In each era it sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 洪武十一年，其王摩那駝喃遣使奉表，貢方物，其後不復 至。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Hongwu, its king Monanuo Nan sent envoys presenting a memorial and local products as tribute; afterward they did not come again.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 11, King Monanuo Nan sent envoys with a memorial and tribute, but no further missions followed.

sentences.zh: 或曰爪哇即阇婆。

translations.literal: Some say Java is Jaraboda.
translations.idiomatic: Some hold that Java and Jaraboda are the same place.

sentences.zh: 然《元史爪哇傳》不言，且曰：「其風俗、物產無所考。」

translations.literal: Yet the "Biography of Java" in the History of Yuan does not say so, and states: "Its customs and products cannot be verified."
translations.idiomatic: Yet the History of Yuan's account of Java does not say so, and remarks: "Its customs and products cannot be verified."

sentences.zh: 太祖時，兩國並時入貢，其王之名不同。

translations.literal: In the time of the Founding Emperor, both states sent tribute at the same time, and the names of their kings differed.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Founding Emperor, both kingdoms sent tribute at the same time, and their kings bore different names.

sentences.zh: 或本為二國，其後為爪哇所滅，然不可考。

translations.literal: Perhaps they were originally two states and Java later destroyed the other, but this cannot be verified.
translations.idiomatic: They may originally have been two kingdoms, with Java later destroying the other—but this cannot be confirmed.

sentences.zh: 蘇吉丹

translations.literal: Sukadana
translations.idiomatic: Sukadana

sentences.zh: 蘇吉丹，爪哇屬國，後訛為思吉港。

translations.literal: Sukadana was a dependency of Java and was later corrupted in name to Sijigang.
translations.idiomatic: Sukadana was a Java dependency whose name was later corrupted to Sijigang.

sentences.zh: 國在山中，止數聚落。

translations.literal: The state lies in the mountains and has only a few settlements.
translations.idiomatic: The kingdom sits in the mountains and consists of only a few settlements.

sentences.zh: 酋居吉力石。

translations.literal: The chieftain dwells at Jilishi.
translations.idiomatic: Its chief resides at Jilishi.

sentences.zh: 其水 潏，舟不可泊。

translations.literal: Its waters are turbulent, and boats cannot anchor.
translations.idiomatic: The waters are rough and ships cannot moor there.

sentences.zh: 商船但往饒洞，其地平衍，國人皆就此貿易。

translations.literal: Merchant ships go only to Raodong; the ground there is level, and the people of the state all trade there.
translations.idiomatic: Merchant vessels call only at Raodong, where the land is flat and all local trade is conducted.

sentences.zh: 其與國有思魯瓦及豬 蠻。

translations.literal: Neighboring states include Siluwa and Zhu Man.
translations.idiomatic: Neighboring peoples include Siluwa and the Zhu Man.

sentences.zh: 豬蠻多盜，華人鮮至。

translations.literal: The Zhu Man are much given to robbery, and Chinese rarely go there.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhu Man are notorious thieves, and Chinese traders seldom visit.

sentences.zh: 碟裡，近爪哇。

translations.literal: Die Li lies near Java.
translations.idiomatic: Die Li lies near Java.

sentences.zh: 永樂三年遣使附其使臣來貢。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongle it sent envoys attached to Java's mission to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle 3 it sent envoys with Java's tribute mission.

sentences.zh: 其地尚釋教，俗淳少訟，物產甚 薄。

translations.literal: The land honors Buddhism; customs are simple and lawsuits are few, and local products are very sparse.
translations.idiomatic: Buddhism is honored there, manners are mild and litigation rare, and local goods are scarce.

sentences.zh: 日羅夏治

translations.literal: Riluoxiaji
translations.idiomatic: Riluoxiaji

sentences.zh: 日羅夏治，近爪哇。

translations.literal: Riluoxiaji lies near Java.
translations.idiomatic: Riluoxiaji lies near Java.

sentences.zh: 永樂三年遣使附其使臣入貢。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongle it sent envoys attached to Java's mission to pay tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle 3 it sent envoys with Java's mission to pay tribute.

sentences.zh: 國小，知種藝，無盜賊。

translations.literal: The state is small; the people know agriculture, and there are no thieves.
translations.idiomatic: It is a small kingdom whose people farm and among whom theft is unknown.

sentences.zh: 亦 尚釋教，所產止蘇木、胡椒。

translations.literal: They also honor Buddhism; their products are only sappanwood and pepper.
translations.idiomatic: They too honor Buddhism and produce only sappanwood and pepper.

sentences.zh: 三佛齊

translations.literal: Srivijaya
translations.idiomatic: Srivijaya

sentences.zh: 三佛齊，古名干陀利。

translations.literal: Srivijaya was anciently called Kantoli.
translations.idiomatic: Srivijaya was anciently known as Kantoli.

sentences.zh: 劉宋孝武帝時，常遣使奉貢。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Xiaowu of Liu Song, envoys were often sent with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xiaowu of Liu Song, it often sent tribute missions.

sentences.zh: 梁武帝時數至。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Wu of Liang, missions came repeatedly.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wu of Liang, missions came again and again.

sentences.zh: 宋名三佛 齊，修貢不絕。

translations.literal: Under Song it was named Srivijaya, and tribute continued without interruption.
translations.idiomatic: The Song knew it as Srivijaya, and tribute never ceased.

sentences.zh: 洪武三年，太祖遣行人趙述詔諭其國。

translations.literal: In the third year of Hongwu, the Founding Emperor dispatched Attendant Zhao Shu to announce instructions to the state.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 3, the Founding Emperor sent Attendant Zhao Shu to announce the court's wishes to the kingdom.

sentences.zh: 明年，其王馬哈剌札八剌卜遣使奉金葉 表，隨入貢黑熊、火雞、孔雀、五色鸚鵡、諸香、苾布、兜羅被諸物。

translations.literal: The next year, its king Maharaja Zapabala sent envoys presenting a gold-leaf memorial and offering black bears, turkeys, peacocks, multicolored parrots, various aromatics, cotton cloth, dharani quilts, and other goods.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, King Maharaja Zapabala sent envoys with a gold-leaf memorial and tribute of black bears, turkeys, peacocks, multicolored parrots, aromatics, cotton cloth, dharani quilts, and other goods.

sentences.zh: 詔賜《大統 歷》及錦綺有差。

translations.literal: An edict bestowed the Datong Calendar and brocades in varying measure.
translations.idiomatic: The court granted the Datong Calendar and brocades in varying amounts.

sentences.zh: 戶部言其貨舶至泉州，宜徵稅，命勿徵。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Revenue said that when its merchant ships reached Quanzhou, taxes ought to be levied; an order was issued not to levy them.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Revenue argued that its merchant ships reaching Quanzhou should be taxed, but the emperor ordered that no tax be collected.

sentences.zh: 六年，王怛麻沙那阿者遣使朝貢，又一表賀明年正旦。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, King Tamasana Aja sent envoys to pay court tribute, and also sent a separate memorial congratulating the court on the coming New Year's Day.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, King Tamasana Aja sent envoys with tribute and a separate memorial congratulating the court on the coming New Year.

sentences.zh: 時其國有三王。

translations.literal: At the time the state had three kings.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the kingdom had three kings.

sentences.zh: 七年， 王麻那哈寶林邦遣使來貢。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, King Manaha Baolinbang sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, King Manaha Baolinbang sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 八年正月復貢。

translations.literal: In the first month of the eighth year tribute came again.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the eighth year they sent tribute again.

sentences.zh: 九月，王僧伽烈宇蘭遣使，隨招諭拂菻 國朝使入貢。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, King Senggalie Yulan sent envoys who accompanied the envoys sent to summon and announce instructions to Fulin to pay court tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, King Senggalie Yulan sent envoys who came with the mission sent to summon Fulin to pay tribute.

sentences.zh: 九年，怛麻沙那阿者卒，子麻那者巫裡嗣。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, Tamasana Aja died, and his son Manazhe Wuli succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year Tamasana Aja died and was succeeded by his son Manazhe Wuli.

sentences.zh: 明年遣使貢犀牛、黑熊、火雞、白 猴、紅緣鸚鵡、龜筒及丁香、米腦諸物。

translations.literal: The next year envoys were sent offering rhinoceroses, black bears, turkeys, white monkeys, red-rimmed parrots, tortoise-shell vessels, cloves, borneol, and other goods.
translations.idiomatic: The following year envoys brought rhinoceroses, black bears, turkeys, white monkeys, red-rimmed parrots, tortoise-shell vessels, cloves, borneol, and other goods.

sentences.zh: 使者言：「嗣子不敢擅立，請命於朝。」

translations.literal: The envoys said: "The successor dares not establish himself on his own and requests appointment from the court."
translations.idiomatic: The envoys said: "The heir dares not take the throne without authorization and asks the court for confirmation."

sentences.zh: 天子嘉其義，命使臣齎印，敕封為三佛齊國王。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven praised this righteousness and ordered the envoys to carry a seal and commanded that he be enfeoffed as king of Srivijaya.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved this conduct and ordered his envoys to carry a seal investing Manazhe Wuli as king of Srivijaya.

sentences.zh: 時爪哇強，已威服三佛齊而役屬之， 聞天朝封為國王與己埒，則大怒，遣人誘朝使邀殺之。

translations.literal: At the time Java was strong and had already overawed Srivijaya and made it a dependent; hearing that the Celestial Court had enfeoffed a king equal to itself, it was greatly enraged and sent men to lure the court envoys and intercept and kill them.
translations.idiomatic: Java was then powerful, had already subjugated Srivijaya, and flew into a rage when it learned the Ming had invested a king equal to its own. It sent men to lure the imperial envoys and kill them.

sentences.zh: 天子亦不能問罪，其國益衰， 貢使遂絕。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven also could not demand punishment, the state grew ever weaker, and tribute envoys ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor could not punish Java, the kingdom declined further, and tribute missions stopped.

sentences.zh: 三十年，禮官以諸蕃久缺貢，奏聞。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year, ritual officials reported to the throne that the foreign states had long failed to send tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year, ritual officials reported that the foreign states had long ceased sending tribute.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「洪武初，諸蕃貢使不絕。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "In the early Hongwu years, tribute envoys from the foreign states did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "In early Hongwu, tribute missions from the foreign states never stopped.

sentences.zh: 邇者安 南、占城、真臘、暹羅、爪哇、大琉球、三佛齊、浡泥、彭亨、百花、蘇門答剌、 西洋等三十國，以胡惟庸作亂，三佛齊乃生間諜，紿我使臣至彼。

translations.literal: Recently Annam, Champa, Khmer, Siam, Java, Great Ryukyu, Srivijaya, Brunei, Pahang, Baihua, Sumatra, the Western Ocean, and thirty other states—because Hu Weiyong raised rebellion, Srivijaya then sent spies and deceived our envoys into coming there.
translations.idiomatic: Recently Annam, Champa, Khmer, Siam, Java, Great Ryukyu, Srivijaya, Brunei, Pahang, Baihua, Sumatra, the Western Ocean, and some thirty other states—after Hu Weiyong's rebellion, Srivijaya sent spies and lured our envoys there.

sentences.zh: 爪哇王聞知，遣 人戒飭，禮送還朝。

translations.literal: When the king of Java heard of it, he sent men to admonish them and escorted them back to court with ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: When the Java king learned of this, he sent men to restrain the offenders and ceremoniously escorted our envoys home.

sentences.zh: 由是商旅阻遏，諸國之意不通。

translations.literal: Because of this, merchants were obstructed and goodwill among the states was cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Trade was disrupted and contact with the kingdoms broke down.

sentences.zh: 惟安南、占城、真臘、暹羅、 大琉球朝貢如故，大琉球且遣子弟入學。

translations.literal: Only Annam, Champa, Khmer, Siam, and Great Ryukyu continued to send tribute as before; Great Ryukyu even sent sons and younger brothers to study.
translations.idiomatic: Only Annam, Champa, Khmer, Siam, and Great Ryukyu kept sending tribute as before; Great Ryukyu even sent princes to study at court.

sentences.zh: 凡諸蕃國使臣來者，皆以禮待之。

translations.literal: All envoys coming from the foreign states were treated with ritual courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Every envoy from the foreign states was received with full ceremony.

sentences.zh: 我視諸 國不薄，未知諸國心若何。

translations.literal: I have not treated the states lightly, yet I do not know what is in their hearts.
translations.idiomatic: I have never slighted these kingdoms, yet I do not know what they think of us.

sentences.zh: 今欲遣使爪哇，恐三佛齊中途沮之。

translations.literal: Now I wish to send envoys to Java, but I fear Srivijaya will obstruct them midway.
translations.idiomatic: I now wish to send envoys to Java, but fear Srivijaya may block them en route.

sentences.zh: 聞三佛齊本爪哇屬 國，可述朕意，移咨暹羅，俾轉達爪哇。」

translations.literal: I hear that Srivijaya was originally a dependency of Java; my wishes may be conveyed in a dispatch to Siam, so that Siam may relay them to Java."
translations.idiomatic: I hear Srivijaya was once Java's dependency. Convey my wishes in a dispatch to Siam and let Siam pass them on to Java."

sentences.zh: 於是部臣移牒曰：「自有天地以來，即 有君臣上下之分，中國四裔之防。

translations.literal: Thereupon the ministry officials issued a dispatch, saying: "Since Heaven and Earth came into being, there have been distinctions between ruler and subject, high and low, and defenses between China and the four quarters.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry then issued a dispatch: "Since the beginning of Heaven and Earth there have been rulers and subjects, high and low, and a boundary between China and the outer world.

sentences.zh: 我朝混一之初，海外諸蕃，莫不來享。

translations.literal: At the beginning of our dynasty's unification, all the overseas foreign states came to pay homage.
translations.idiomatic: When our dynasty first united the realm, every overseas state came to pay homage.

sentences.zh: 豈意胡惟 庸謀亂，三佛齊遂生異心，紿我信使，肆行巧詐。

translations.literal: Who would have thought that Hu Weiyong would plot rebellion, that Srivijaya would then harbor a different heart, deceive our envoys, and act with wilful fraud.
translations.idiomatic: Who could have expected Hu Weiyong's rebellion, after which Srivijaya turned disloyal, deceived our envoys, and practiced deceit?

sentences.zh: 我聖天子一以仁義待諸蕃，何諸 蕃敢背大恩，失君臣之禮。

translations.literal: Our sage Son of Heaven has treated all the foreign states solely with benevolence and righteousness—how dare the foreign states turn against great favor and abandon the rites between ruler and subject.
translations.idiomatic: Our sage emperor has treated every foreign state with benevolence and righteousness—how dare they repay such grace by violating the bond between ruler and subject?

sentences.zh: 倘天子震怒，遣一偏將將十萬之師，恭行天罰，易如覆 手，爾諸蕃何不思之甚。

translations.literal: If the Son of Heaven were roused to anger and sent one partial general with a hundred thousand troops to reverently execute Heaven's punishment, it would be as easy as turning the hand over—how deeply unthinking you foreign states are.
translations.idiomatic: Should the emperor grow angry and send a single general with a hundred thousand men to execute Heaven's punishment, it would be as easy as turning one's hand—how little you foreign states have thought.

sentences.zh: 我聖天子嘗曰：『安南、占城、真臘、暹羅、大琉球皆修 臣職，惟三佛齊梗我聲教。

translations.literal: Our sage Son of Heaven once said: 'Annam, Champa, Khmer, Siam, and Great Ryukyu all observe their duties as subjects; only Srivijaya obstructs my civilizing influence.
translations.idiomatic: Our sage emperor once said: 'Annam, Champa, Khmer, Siam, and Great Ryukyu all fulfill their duties; only Srivijaya resists our civilizing influence.

sentences.zh: 彼以蕞爾之國，敢倔強不服，自取滅亡。』

translations.literal: That tiny state dares to be stubborn and disobedient and brings destruction upon itself.'
translations.idiomatic: That petty kingdom dares defy us and invites its own ruin.'

sentences.zh: 爾暹羅恪守 臣節，天朝眷禮有加，可轉達爪哇，令以大義告諭三佛齊，誠能省愆從善，則禮待 如初。」

translations.literal: You Siam have kept your subject's duty; the Celestial Court's favor and courtesy toward you have been abundant. Relay this to Java and have Java instruct Srivijaya in righteousness; if Srivijaya can reflect on its faults and turn to goodness, it will be treated with ritual courtesy as before."
translations.idiomatic: Siam has kept faith as a subject, and the court has shown you special favor. Pass this on to Java and let Java admonish Srivijaya in the name of righteousness. If Srivijaya repents and reforms, it will be treated as before."

sentences.zh: 時爪哇已破三佛齊，據其國，改其名曰舊港，三佛齊遂亡。

translations.literal: At that time Java had already broken Srivijaya, occupied its land, changed its name to Old Port, and Srivijaya perished.
translations.idiomatic: By then Java had already destroyed Srivijaya, seized its territory, renamed it Old Port, and Srivijaya was no more.

sentences.zh: 國中大亂，爪 哇亦不能盡有其地，華人流寓者往往起而據之。

translations.literal: Great disorder arose within the state; Java also could not fully hold all the land, and Chinese who had settled there often rose up and seized portions of it.
translations.idiomatic: The country fell into chaos. Java could not hold all the territory, and Chinese settlers often seized portions for themselves.

sentences.zh: 有梁道明者，廣州南海縣人，久居 其國，閩、粵軍民泛海從之者數千家，推道明為首，雄視一方。

translations.literal: There was a man named Liang Daoming, a native of Nanhai County in Guangzhou, who had long lived in the state; several thousand families of Fujian and Guangdong soldiers and civilians who crossed the sea followed him, and they made Daoming their head, dominating one region.
translations.idiomatic: One Liang Daoming, a native of Nanhai County in Guangzhou, had long lived there. Several thousand Fujian and Guangdong families who crossed the sea followed him, made him their leader, and dominated the region.

sentences.zh: 會指揮孫鉉使海 外，遇其子，挾與俱來。

translations.literal: When Commander Sun Xuan was sent on a mission overseas, he met Daoming's son, took him along, and brought him back.
translations.idiomatic: When Commander Sun Xuan went on a mission overseas, he met Daoming's son, brought him along, and returned with him.

sentences.zh: 永樂三年，成祖以行人譚勝受與道明同邑，命偕千戶楊信等齎敕招之。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongle, the Yongle Emperor, because Attendant Tan Shengshou was from the same district as Daoming, ordered him to go together with Thousand-Commander Yang Xin and others, bearing an edict to summon him.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle 3, because Attendant Tan Shengshou came from Daoming's home district, the Yongle Emperor ordered him to go with Thousand-Commander Yang Xin and others, bearing an edict to summon Daoming.

sentences.zh: 道明及 其黨鄭伯可隨入朝，貢方物，受賜而還。

translations.literal: Daoming and his follower Zheng Boke followed them to court, offered local products, received gifts, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Daoming and his follower Zheng Boke came to court, presented tribute, received gifts, and went home.

sentences.zh: 四年，舊港頭目陳祖義遣子士良，道明遣從子觀政並來朝。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Old Port chief Chen Zuyi sent his son Shiliang, and Daoming sent his nephew Guanzheng; both came to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, Old Port chief Chen Zuyi sent his son Shiliang and Daoming sent his nephew Guanzheng; both came to court.

sentences.zh: 祖義，亦廣東人，雖朝貢，而為盜海上，貢使往來者苦之。

translations.literal: Zuyi, also a native of Guangdong, though he paid court tribute, plundered on the sea, and tribute envoys traveling back and forth suffered from him.
translations.idiomatic: Zuyi, also a Guangdong native, paid tribute but robbed the seas, and traveling tribute envoys suffered from him.

sentences.zh: 五年，鄭和自西洋還，遣人招諭之。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Zheng He returned from the Western Ocean and sent men to summon and instruct him.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Zheng He returned from the Western Ocean and sent men to summon him.

sentences.zh: 祖義詐降，潛謀邀劫。

translations.literal: Zuyi feigned surrender and secretly plotted to intercept and rob.
translations.idiomatic: Zuyi feigned surrender and secretly plotted an ambush.

sentences.zh: 有施進者，告於和。

translations.literal: A man named Shi Jinqing reported this to He.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Jinqing reported the plot to Zheng He.

sentences.zh: 祖義來襲被擒，獻於朝，伏誅。

translations.literal: Zuyi came to attack, was captured, presented at court, and executed.
translations.idiomatic: Zuyi attacked, was captured, sent to court, and executed.

sentences.zh: 時進卿適遣婿丘彥誠朝貢，命設舊港宣慰司，以進卿為使，錫誥印及冠帶。

translations.literal: At that time Jinqing had just sent his son-in-law Qiu Yancheng with tribute; the court ordered the establishment of the Old Port Pacification Commission, appointed Jinqing commissioner, and granted a patent of appointment, seal, and official cap and belt.
translations.idiomatic: Jinqing had just sent his son-in-law Qiu Yancheng with tribute; the court established the Old Port Pacification Commission, appointed Jinqing commissioner, and granted a patent, seal, and official regalia.

sentences.zh: 自是，屢入貢。

translations.literal: From this time they repeatedly entered with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: From then on they sent tribute repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 然進卿雖受朝命，猶服屬爪哇，其地狹小，非故時三佛齊也。

translations.literal: Yet although Jinqing received the court's commission, he still acknowledged Java's authority; the territory was narrow and small, not the Srivijaya of former times.
translations.idiomatic: Yet although Jinqing held a court commission, he still acknowledged Java; the territory was small, not the Srivijaya of old.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，進卿子濟孫告父訃，乞嗣職，許之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year Jinqing's son Jisun reported his father's death and begged to succeed to the office; this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: In year 22 Jinqing's son Jisun reported his father's death and begged to succeed; the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 洪熙元年遣使入貢，訴舊印為火毀，帝命重給。

translations.literal: In the first year of Hongxi envoys were sent with tribute, reporting that the old seal had been destroyed by fire; the Emperor ordered it to be reissued.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongxi 1 envoys came with tribute, reporting that the old seal had been destroyed by fire; the Emperor ordered a new one issued.

sentences.zh: 其後，朝貢漸稀。

translations.literal: After that, tribute missions gradually grew rare.
translations.idiomatic: After that, tribute missions grew increasingly rare.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖末，廣東大盜張璉作亂，官軍已報克獲。

translations.literal: At the end of the Jiajing reign, the great bandit of Guangdong, Zhang Lian, raised rebellion, and the government troops had already reported his capture.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Jiajing reign, the Guangdong bandit Zhang Lian rebelled, and government troops reported that he had been captured.

sentences.zh: 萬曆五年商人詣舊港者，見璉列 肆為蕃舶長，漳、泉人多附之，猶中國市舶官雲。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Wanli, merchants who went to Old Port saw Lian set up shops as chief of the foreign merchant ships; many from Zhangzhou and Quanzhou attached themselves to him, much like a Chinese superintendent of merchant shipping.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli 5, merchants reaching Old Port found Zhang Lian running shops as chief of the foreign merchant fleet. Many men from Zhangzhou and Quanzhou followed him, much like a Chinese port superintendent.

sentences.zh: 其地為諸蕃要會，在爪哇之西，順風八晝夜可至。

translations.literal: The place is a great meeting point of the foreign states, lying west of Java; with a fair wind one can reach it in eight day-and-night journeys.
translations.idiomatic: The site is a major crossroads of the foreign states, west of Java—eight days' sail with a fair wind.

sentences.zh: 轄十五洲，土沃宜稼。

translations.literal: It governs fifteen districts, and the soil is fertile and suited to crops.
translations.idiomatic: It controls fifteen districts on fertile land well suited to agriculture.

sentences.zh: 語云： 「一年種穀，三年生金。」

translations.literal: A saying goes: "Plant grain for one year, and gold grows for three."
translations.idiomatic: A proverb says: "Sow grain for a year, and gold accrues for three."

sentences.zh: 言收穫盛而貿金多也。

translations.literal: This means harvests are abundant and trade in gold is great.
translations.idiomatic: This means harvests are rich and the gold trade flourishes.

sentences.zh: 俗富好淫。

translations.literal: The custom is wealth and fondness for licentiousness.
translations.idiomatic: The people are wealthy and prone to licentiousness.

sentences.zh: 習於水戰，鄰國畏之。

translations.literal: They are practiced in naval warfare, and neighboring states fear them.
translations.idiomatic: They are skilled in naval warfare, and neighboring states fear them.

sentences.zh: 地多水，惟部領陸居，庶民皆水居。

translations.literal: The land is mostly water; only the chiefs dwell on land, while common people all live on the water.
translations.idiomatic: Water covers most of the land; only the chiefs live ashore, while commoners dwell on the water.

sentences.zh: 編筏築室，繫之於樁。

translations.literal: They weave rafts and build houses, tying them to piles.
translations.idiomatic: They weave rafts into dwellings and moor them to piles.

sentences.zh: 水漲則筏浮，無沉溺患。

translations.literal: When the water rises the rafts float, and there is no danger of sinking.
translations.idiomatic: When the waters rise the rafts float with them, so there is no risk of foundering.

sentences.zh: 欲徙則拔樁去之，不費財力。

translations.literal: If they wish to move, they pull up the piles and go, without expense of wealth or labor.
translations.idiomatic: To relocate they simply pull up the piles and go, at little cost in money or effort.

sentences.zh: 下稱其上曰詹卑，猶國君也。

translations.literal: Those below call their superiors zhanbei, like a ruler of the state.
translations.idiomatic: Subordinates address their superiors as zhanbei, much as one would a sovereign.

sentences.zh: 後大酋所居，即號詹卑 國，改故都為舊港。

translations.literal: Later the place where the great chief dwelt was called the state of Zhanbei, and the former capital was renamed Old Port.
translations.idiomatic: Later the great chief's seat was styled the state of Zhanbei, and the former capital was renamed Old Port.

sentences.zh: 初本富饒，自爪哇破滅，後漸致蕭索，商舶鮮至。

translations.literal: At first it was truly rich, but since Java destroyed and extinguished it, it gradually grew desolate and merchant ships rarely came.
translations.idiomatic: It was once genuinely prosperous, but after Java destroyed it the region gradually declined, and merchant vessels seldom called.

sentences.zh: 其他風俗、 物產，具詳《宋史》。

translations.literal: Other customs and products are fully detailed in the History of Song.
translations.idiomatic: Other customs and products are set forth in full in the History of Song.
